sections.heading: Welcome to Explora Atacama
sections.text:
Welcome to Explora Atacama
Experience the best of Chile’s surreal desert landscape at Explora Atacama, our multi-award-winning lodge near the oasis town of San Pedro de Atacama. Surrounded by the wild beauty of the vast Atacama Desert — salt flats, volcanoes, geysers, windswept dunes and more — discover a contemporary retreat with every comfort in mind. Enjoy a unique culinary experience, four pools and a spa, and stargazing from our onsite Observatory. Then venture out on horseback from Explora’s own stables, bike or hike the Altiplano with views of the Valley of the Moon, and soak in the natural hot springs, exclusively located in Explora’s Puritama Conservation Reserve.

sections.heading: Stay in a Stunning Oasis

Stay in a Stunning Oasis
With an awe-inspiring architecture to match its vast desert surrounds, Explora Atacama is a true oasis amidst the rugged landscapes of the Atacama Desert. At our 50-room lodge near the historic town of San Pedro de Atacama, discover an elevated stay beyond compare, including all meals, spa facilities with a sauna and four pools, and our own onsite observatory and horseback riding stables.
VIEW LODGE

sections.heading: Embark on Desert Explorations
sections.text:
Embark on Desert Explorations
You’re invited to choose from nearly 50 guided Explorations at Explora Atacama, all included as part of your stay. Led by our own expertly trained guides, these experiences and Explora-only adventures include horseback riding, biking, hiking and high-elevation climbs across the soul-stirring geology of the otherworldly Atacama.
Every Exploration is also customized to match your interests and fitness levels, ensuring an unforgettable adventure made just for you.

Enjoy Authentic Cuisine
At Explora Atacama, we present an authentic, handcrafted daily menu that highlights the bold flavors and rich culinary traditions of Chile’s Atacama region. Savor fresh locally inspired dishes while enjoying spectacular views from our intimate dining room, where every meal is an experience in itself.

sections.text:
Step Inside Our Atacama Desert Lodge
Situated on a pristine 42-acre (17-hectare) desert estate near San Pedro de Atacama, the 50-room Explora Atacama offers an elevated experience in the middle of the world’s highest and driest desert. Designed to match this spectacular destination and immerse you fully in it, the lodge offers an award-winning architecture, inviting rooms for rest and rejuvenation, a tranquil spa and multiple pools, and a world-class Observatory for taking in dazzling Atacama night skies.

Prime Desert Location
Explora Atacama boasts a perch on the beautiful Ayllu de Larache, surrounded by the sand dunes and high-elevation parklands of enchanting San Pedro de Atacama, the Atacama’s most famous oasis. The lodge also affords easy access to the many wonders of the desert and the high-elevation Altiplano, including the nearby Altiplanic Lagoons and ancient Pukará de Quitor archeological site.

sections.heading: Architecture Inspired by Nature
sections.text:
Architecture Inspired by Nature
Designed by famed Chilean architect José Cruz Ovalle, our award-winning lodge embodies a commitment to sustainability and immersion in nature, creating an unforgettable experience for guests who want to authentically connect with Atacama’s desert landscapes. Soaring spaces, sweeping views and locally sourced furnishings define the grounds and interiors, while common areas, such as the dining room and lounge spaces, invite opportunities to enjoy relaxing, socializing, or quiet contemplation.

sections.heading: Scenic Spa, Pools & More
sections.text:
Scenic Spa, Pools & More
Surrounded by tall pampas grass and Atacama flora, our four interconnected pools are the perfect place to relax and soak in the quiet of the desert. Each pool offers a different experience, including a pool warmed to 77–82°F (25–28° C). Nearby in a traditional adobe house, visit our spa with a range of treatments as well as a sauna, steam baths and outdoor hot tubs.

sections.heading: World-Class Observatory

World-Class Observatory
San Pedro de Atacama is world-renowned for its clear skies and incredible stargazing. The exceptional clarity of its sky has attracted cutting-edge observatories, including ALMA with its groundbreaking astronomical discoveries. See these dazzling night skies from our very own onsite Observatory, with guided star tours and Explorations that reveal the Milky Way, planets and endless constellations.

sections.heading: Flexible Experiences Customized Daily
sections.text:
Flexible Experiences Customized Daily
Our Explorations feature classic routes to iconic sites as well as Signature Explorations, designed and operated exclusively by Explora in the region’s most remote and pristine locations. Every adventure is customized daily to match with your skills and interests — something you’ll experience every evening, when your Explora guide meets with you to tailor the next day’s Explorations to your preferences.
Explorations are limited to a group size of no more than eight guests to allow for a more personal atmosphere and in-depth discovery. Privately guided Explorations are available at an additional cost.

Led by Explora’s Exclusively Trained Guides
Deeply familiar with the region and its traditions, are local guides have an unyielding passion and knowledge for the Atacama and the magical landscapes we explore. They’re trained at our own School of Guides and fluent in Spanish and English. They are also keenly aware of the fragility of these unique places and share in our advocacy for the conservation of this special desert’s many treasures.

sections.heading: Discover the Best of the Atacama Desert
sections.text:
Discover the Best of the Atacama Desert
Choose from 49 in-depth Explorations across four unique Andean zones. These Atacama adventures and experiences include hiking the Cordillera de la Sal with views to the Valley of the Moon, horseback riding over breathtaking desert dunes and swims in private hot springs at Explora’s own Puritama Conservation Reserve.

sections.heading: 1. Cuenca del salar
sections.text:
Explore by: Hike Overland Bike Horseback Ride E-Bike Sky High Mountain Ascent
Explore 52 explorations located in the 5 unique Atacama zones:
1. Cuenca del salar
Geometric and seemingly infinite, the Atacama salt flat abruptly interrupts the desert’s chromatic continuum. The crunch of salt under every footstep is swept into silence by the wind, and all that’s left is to go deeper into the territory around you. The lowest part of this area corresponds to the Atacama Salt Flat (2350 m.a.s.l.) itself, an endorheic basin that once accumulated the waters and sediments from volcanoes and mountains over millions of years. Today it hosts a complex ecosystem, including half of the world’s flamingo species. Also within this Exploration zone, the Salt Mountain range rises to the west of the salt flat in a geological spectacle, as crusts of sediments crown the rugged mountains that frame the desert. Finally, we recommend exploring the Oasis of San Pedro, which stands as a beacon of life and local traditions kept alive by its people
Explore by: 
View Cuenca del salar Explorations 
2. Quebradas Intermedias
As if sliced off from the desert’s mantle, the ravines in this zone were created over millions of years by the forces of water and wind. Plunging into the abyss, they are sculptures that only time could shape. Numerous ravines connect the Altiplano and Salt Flat Basin zones, crisscrossing the ascent while volcanic stonewalls and brooks lined with wild grass species modestly irrigate the surrounding land, making room for medicinal plants and flowers which have been used by local shepherding communities for centuries. The Domeyko Mountain Range, located in this zone, hosts wildlife and cultural heritage alike, with guanacos and ancient petroglyphs doting certain hillsides. The ravines offer a cradle for life to flourish in, as is the case of the Puritama Natural Reserve, where a series of hot springs irrigate and sustain a series of ecosystems within.

Today it hosts a complex ecosystem, including half of the world’s flamingo species. Also within this Exploration zone, the Salt Mountain range rises to the west of the salt flat in a geological spectacle, as crusts of sediments crown the rugged mountains that frame the desert. As if sliced off from the desert’s mantle, the ravines in this zone were created over millions of years by the forces of water and wind. Plunging into the abyss, they are sculptures that only time could shape. Numerous ravines connect the Altiplano and Salt Flat Basin zones, crisscrossing the ascent while volcanic stonewalls and brooks lined with wild grass species modestly irrigate the surrounding land, making room for medicinal plants and flowers which have been used by local shepherding communities for centuries. The Domeyko Mountain Range, located in this zone, hosts wildlife and cultural heritage alike, with guanacos and ancient petroglyphs doting certain hillsides. The ravines offer a cradle for life to flourish in, as is the case of the Puritama Natural Reserve, where a series of hot springs irrigate and sustain a series of ecosystems within.

The Altiplano exists up there, somewhere between the mountains and the sky. Within, a whole new world silently awaits the intrepid explorers that venture its way. For us, this is a territory that words simply fall short of. The Altiplano zone –or Puna as it is known locally– stretches between 3800 and 4300 m.a.s.l. It is an elevated plateau, crowned by imposing mountains, volcanoes and geysers. Lack of oxygen, intense sunlight and extreme temperatures keep this unique territory safe, calling only those who are drawn to unusual beauty.

These colossal massifs not only hoard minerals, but also encompass cultural expressions of people past and present. Axes of mystery, Atacama’s mountains frame its territory, remaining vigilant of all whom explore it. The best views of Atacama can be found by reaching the peaks of the Licancabur Volcano along with the Kimal, Toco, Láscar, Corona, Soquete, Sairecabur and Colorado mountains – summits that scrape the skies at over 5000 m.a.s.l. Though spectacular, this altitude level requires physical stamina and preparation, and is therefore not for the faint of heart. The rewards, however, are worth the patience and dedication: a unique encounter with the world from above

Atacama’s night skies are a constant spectacle. When night falls, the sky becomes alive with the infinite powder of the Milky Way or Celestial River, as it is known in Atacama. Star-gazing has been a pastime of humanity since the dawn of time, as our forefathers often looked to the skies for divine answers. Atacama’s night skies’ sheer definition allows gazers to draw their own constellations and meaning from beyond our planet and even our galaxy. At the center of the Milky Way lies the Yakana or constellation of the Llama, seen breastfeeding its newborn calf. To its right are the Partridge, the Frog and the Serpent constellations, which guide the Andean shepherds and farmers, protecting them seasonal floods.

sections.heading: Climate
sections.text:
Climate
Situated in one of the driest regions on Earth, San Pedro de Atacama is defined by its extreme aridity and striking landscapes. Here, the climate is remarkably stable, with almost no rainfall throughout the year. Days are typically warm, while nights can be cold, with significant temperature drops after sunset.
The desert’s unique environment supports a surprising diversity of life, with flora and fauna adapted to thrive in these harsh conditions. San Pedro de Atacama is also renowned for its crystal-clear skies, making it one of the best places in the world for stargazing, offering unparalleled views of the night sky.

FAQs
LOGISTICS & PLANNING
WHAT’S THE BEST TIME OF YEAR TO VISIT THE ATACAMA?
The Atacama Desert is a year-round destination, with each season offering unique conditions that shape the travel experience. In the summer months (December to February), temperatures during the day are warm and pleasant, but this is also when there’s a slightly higher chance of rain due to the so-called Altiplanic Winter—short, sporadic showers that can bring dramatic skies and rare desert blooms. In contrast, winter (June to August) brings colder nights, often with temperatures dropping below freezing, especially at higher altitudes, while daytime remains sunny and dry. Spring and fall offer a balance of mild weather and fewer crowds. Regardless of when you visit, the Atacama’s striking landscapes, starry skies, and otherworldly beauty make it an unforgettable destination any time of year.
HOW MANY DAYS SHOULD I SPEND IN THE ATACAMA DESERT?
To truly connect with the vastness and diversity of the Atacama Desert, we recommend staying for at least five nights. This allows enough time to explore a variety of landscapes—from salt flats and geysers to canyons and lunar-like valleys—without feeling rushed. With six or more nights, you’ll have the opportunity to go deeper into the territory, reaching the high plateau, visiting remote lagoons, or even ascending one of the region’s iconic volcanoes. A longer stay also means you can enjoy the pace of exploration while taking in the desert’s silence, colors, and night skies at a more immersive rhythm.

faqs.q: What’s the best time of year to visit the Atacama?
faqs.a: The Atacama Desert is a year-round destination, with each season offering unique conditions that shape the travel experience. In the summer months (December to February), temperatures during the day are warm and pleasant, but this is also when there’s a slightly higher chance of rain due to the so-called Altiplanic Winter—short, sporadic showers that can bring dramatic skies and rare desert blooms. In contrast, winter (June to August) brings colder nights, often with temperatures dropping below freezing, especially at higher altitudes, while daytime remains sunny and dry. Spring and fall offer a balance of mild weather and fewer crowds. Regardless of when you visit, the Atacama’s striking landscapes, starry skies, and otherworldly beauty make it an unforgettable destination any time of year.

faqs.q: How many days should I spend in the Atacama Desert?
faqs.a: To truly connect with the vastness and diversity of the Atacama Desert, we recommend staying for at least five nights. This allows enough time to explore a variety of landscapes—from salt flats and geysers to canyons and lunar-like valleys—without feeling rushed. With six or more nights, you’ll have the opportunity to go deeper into the territory, reaching the high plateau, visiting remote lagoons, or even ascending one of the region’s iconic volcanoes. A longer stay also means you can enjoy the pace of exploration while taking in the desert’s silence, colors, and night skies at a more immersive rhythm.

faqs.q: Is credit card acceptance widespread or should I bring cash?
faqs.a: Credit cards are widely accepted at Explora and in most shops, restaurants, and services in downtown San Pedro de Atacama. However, it’s a good idea to carry some cash for small purchases at local markets, artisan stands, or rural communities, where card payment may not be available. Cash is also useful for tipping staff at the Explora lodge, should you wish to do so. That said, there’s no need to worry about paying for additional services during your stay—everything at the lodge is included as part of the all-inclusive experience.

faqs.q: How extreme is the temperature difference between day and night in Explora Atacama Lodge?
faqs.a: During winter, the temperatures in Explora’s Atacama Desert Lodge fluctuate between -10°C (14°F) at night and 20°C (68°F) in daytime. During summer, the temperatures fluctuate between 10°C (50°F) at night and 30°C (86°F) in daytime.

faqs.q: Are there vegetarian/vegan food options available?
faqs.a: Yes! There are vegetarian/vegan food options available in every Explora destination. If you have any dietary preferences or restrictions, please contact our reserves team before your arrival.

faqs.q: Do I need to make restaurant reservations in advance?
faqs.a: Theres is no need to make restaurant reservations in advance if you are staying in any Explora Lodge, our travelers are always considered in every meal, it is part of the all-inclusive service we offer.

faqs.q: What are the must-see attractions in the Atacama Desert?
faqs.a: Explora has plenty of “must-see” attractions that you certainly cannot miss, however, it will depend on your preferences and experience, as you can choose from almost 50 guided explorations included in your stay, from a visit to the observatory to see a wonderful starry night to a panoramic view from the peaks of different mountains.

faqs.q: What is the best way to experience stargazing in the Atacama?
faqs.a: The Atacama Desert is world-renowned for its clear skies and minimal light pollution, making it one of the best places on Earth for stargazing. At Explora, you can take this experience to the next level with access to our private observatory, designed specifically for astronomical observation. Accompanied by expert guides, you’ll have the chance to view constellations, planets, and deep-sky objects through high-quality telescopes—an awe-inspiring experience that reveals the full beauty of the desert’s night skies.

faqs.q: Can I visit Bolivia’s Salar de Uyuni from the Explora Atacama Lodge?
faqs.a: Yes, it is possible to visit Bolivia’s Salar de Uyuni from Explora Atacama through a special overland journey designed by Explora. However, this experience must be booked separately and confirmed prior to your arrival at the lodge. Due to the logistics involved, it is not possible to arrange this trip once you are already at the lodge. We recommend planning ahead to ensure availability and a seamless travel experience across the border into Bolivia.

faqs.q: How far in advance should I book with Explora?
faqs.a: We recommend booking your stay at least 60 days in advance to ensure availability and allow enough time to plan every detail of your trip. However, for greater flexibility and peace of mind—especially during peak travel periods—reserving 6 months ahead is ideal. Whether you’re traveling in high or low season, early booking helps us prepare everything to deliver the seamless, immersive experience Explora is known for.

faqs.q: Does Explora offer private experiences or only group activities?
faqs.a: Yes, Explora offers private experiences with an additional cost and coordinated in advance.

faqs.q: Does Explora offer transportation from the airport?
faqs.a: Yes, Explora provides complimentary transportation at preset schedules to and from the nearest airport as part of your all-inclusive experience. Upon arrival, a member of our team will be waiting to welcome you and ensure a smooth transfer to the lodge. Likewise, at the end of your stay, we’ll coordinate your return journey to the airport so you can travel comfortably and on time. All transfers are scheduled based on your flight details and arranged in advance for your convenience.

sections.heading: Explora Ramaditas Mountain Lodge
sections.text:
Explora Ramaditas Mountain Lodge
Set amidst shimmering, multi-colored lagoons, our modern four-room Ramaditas lodge Bolivia combines comfortable common areas and Bolivian-sourced materials in the heart of the Altiplano. From here, experience geysers, lagoons, rock formations, ancient trade routes, and vast Andean valleys—along with a striking perch and wall-to-wall windows that invite the landscape in. Elevation: 13,370 feet (4,075 meters).

sections.heading: Explora Chituca Mountain Lodge
sections.text:
Explora Chituca Mountain Lodge
Once a lookout for shepherds, our four-room Mountain Lodge in Chituca offers panoramic views of the Altiplano. The surrounding area is rich with ancient settlements, vibrant quinoa fields, and storied villages. Unwind in the cozy lounge and dining area, before retreating to a comfortably minimalist room with stunning views over the distant salt flat. Elevation: 12,244 feet (3,732 meters).

sections.heading: Explora Jirira Lodge
sections.text:
Explora Jirira Lodge
At the foot of the Tunupa Volcano on the northern edge of the Uyuni Salt Flats, our six-room Jirira lodge offers a spectacular view of the world’s largest salt flat. The setting is perfect for exploration: climb the colorful slopes of Tunupa, visit the salt flat’s islands, and discover local villages, wetlands, and nearby archaeological sites. Elevation: 12,077 feet (3,681 meters).

sections.heading: Modern Prefab Design
sections.text:
Modern Prefab Design
Explora’s three mountain lodges in Ramaditas, Chituca, and Jirira were designed by Chilean architect Max Núñez. His objective: develop lodging with exceptional minimal impact that raises awareness of the surrounding territory. Discover striking modular designs hoovering above extraordinary places and 100-percent prefabricated and entirely “reversible” construction that allows for future repurposable use.

sections.text:

Explore 30 destinations located in the 5 unique Uyuni Salt Flats & Atacama zones:
1. Chituca
Chituca was once a shepherding settlement, boasting impressive views of both the Altiplano and the salt flat. This mountain home offers excellent opportunities to further discover the cultural landscapes around it, exploring local villages while also delving further into archaeological understanding. Explorations take different shapes and durations: one option is to follow the shepherds’ paths, once used by the area’s original inhabitants as trading routes with other villages. Another alternative is to visit the secluded village of San Pedro de Quemes, an old Spanish settlement with panoramic views of the Altiplano and salt flat, exploring archaeological sites and human settlements that use quinoa cultivation as a main source of income.

We invite our travelers to stay in the Altiplano area for as long a possible, so as to reacquaint with a slower pace of mind and body which is rarely found elsewhere.

How to Get Here
From Calama: Once in Santiago de Chile International Airport (SCL), you need to take a 2-hour connection flight to the northern city of Calama (CJC). From Uyuni: To start this travesía in Bolivia, you will need to reach the Internacional Joya Andina Airport (UYU). We will pick you up there to begin the journey.

To apply for a Bolivian visa, ensure you have the following documents prepared: Visa application sworn statement Color photocopy of your valid passport (must have at least six months of validity remaining) Two passport-sized, color photos with a white background Color photocopy of your Yellow Fever vaccination certificate Photocopy of your Explora booking confirmation (must include your name) Photocopy of your flight tickets out of Bolivia, showing your name, flight details, and date. Important Notes: All cash must be in USD, new, untorn, and free from any markings or writing. Each traveler must have a separate copy of the required documents, even if traveling as a couple or family. Altitude
During the journey through the Altiplano, the altitudes fluctuate between 3,600 and 4,700 m.a.s.l. (11,811 and 15,419 f.a.s.l)
Uyuni is located at 4,700 m.a.s.l (15,400 f.a.s.l.) while the oasis of San Pedro is located at 2,500 m.a.s.l. (8,200 f.a.s.l.) Iquique is at sea level.
During the first day of the travesía, we will only take small walks that won’t require an important physical effort in order to gradually acclimate our bodies to the altitude before the rest of the journey.
Climate
With more than 90% of sunny days, San Pedro de Atacama has a privileged weather all year-round. During the day, temperature goes from 8°C to 23°C in winter (June to September) and from 12°C to 28°C in summer (December to March).
Uyuni´s weather is as dry as San Pedro’s but, because it is at higher levels, it is usually colder. During the winter (June to September), daily temperatures fluctuate between 2°C and 18°C, and during the summer (September to December) between 5°C and 20°C. Temperatures at night can be as low as -20°C.
Between December and March, the area if affected by “The Altiplano Summer” whose heavy rains deeply damage the tracks.
Other Requirements
To be healthy enough to be able to face heights and fluctuating temperatures. Adventure and good spirit.
Some people are sleep deprived when in altitude. Only in that case, we advise you to bring some products that can help you sleep.
Wifi and Voltage
Because we are in remote areas, Wi-Fi access is limited.
The voltage in our Travesía Atacama & Uyuni is 220V.
Tips
Tips are voluntary.
If you wish to leave any, you can do so at the hotel reception at the end of your stay. It will be distributed among all those who contributed to making your trip a unique experience. We suggest leaving USD 100 per day per room.

explorations.name: Jirira
explorations.text: We will start our hike from the lodge, descending towards the Salar while surrounding the peninsula. We will enjoy impressive views of the Tunupa volcano, walk among a great number of cacti and unique rock outcroppings in the area, as well as see flamingos and the K'ajchi Island. Then, we will round the peninsula to climb up the other side and finally return back to the lodge.

explorations.name: Isla K´ajchi
explorations.text: Departing from the lodge, we will head towards the Salar on bicycles. During the summer season, we will pass through the quinoa plantations before entering the Salar through the main entrance. We will experience the unique sensation of cycling through this incomparable landscape with stunning views of the Tunupa volcano. We will arrive at K'ajchi Island, where we will have the option of turning back or walking to the highest point for an elevated view of the Salar. On the island, we will enjoy a snack before continuing our exploration, perfectly timed with the sunset. Finally, we will return to the lodge by bike or jeep.

explorations.name: Wila Khollu
explorations.text: We will start our hike from the lodge towards the summit of Cerro Wila Khollu. Along the way, we will come across a Pirwa, an ancient rock shelter used primarily for storing potato crops, as well as archaeological remains. From the summit, we will enjoy a spectacular view of the Tunupa volcano and the Uyuni salt flats. We will return by the same path until we reach the lodge again.

explorations.name: Trayecto Overland & Yardangs
explorations.text: We will depart by vehicle from Ramaditas towards the Laguna Pastos Grandes area, where we will hike for 4 hours around wetlands and incredible rock formations called Yardangs. ## OVERVIEW
Discover Travesía Atacama-Uyuni
An exclusive journey from Chile’s Atacama Desert to Bolivia’s salt flats, Travesìa Atacama-Uyuni offers travelers a rare opportunity to transit a spectacular and otherworldly high-altitude route in surprising comfort, and entirely under the wing of seasoned Explora guides. On our nine-day travesìa — the Spanish word for long crossing — venture over 300 miles through some of the most remote and awe-inspiring landscapes of the Altiplano, including the Laguna Colorado with its pink flamingos, towering Irruputuncu volcano, and endless, staggeringly bright Salar de Uyuni salt flat.

The all-inclusive experience includes every elevated meal and drinks, stays exclusively at Explora lodges, transit by comfortable 4×4 vehicle, and unforgettable Explorations in ethereal Andean landscapes.

In Chile, your journey begins with a stay near San Pedro de Atacama at stunning Explora Atacama, where acclimatization can include Explorations to private hot springs, treatments at the spa, and stargazing at our own observatory. In Bolivia, discover Explora’s three intimate, minimalist mountain lodges in Ramaditas, Chituca and Jirira, designed by an award-winning architect and surrounded by nothing but vast expanses of natural beauty.
VIEW LODGES
Discover Immersive Explorations
Traversing the world’s most extreme and extraordinary landscapes includes an endless supply of expertly guided Explorations. Led exclusively by Explora guides and customized daily to match your interest and fitness levels, excursions and experiences span three different altitude zones from Atacama to Uyuni, and everything from hikes and bike rides over salt flats to high-mountain ascents to famed volcanos.

## ITINERARIES
Join an Expertly Designed Itinerary from Atacama to Uyuni
Designed by Explora’s experts to authentically reveal the high desert and infinite salt flats, our nine-day Travesía Atacama-Uyuni journey invites you to discover two of the most fascinating places on Earth in the journey of a lifetime.
Begin this all-inclusive experience with four nights at Explora Atacama, our multi-award-winning lodge near San Pedro De Atacama where countless expertly guided desert Explorations await. Properly acclimatized, journey from here across the remote Altiplano to Bolivia, safely transiting 338 miles (544 km) in a comfortable, satellite-equipped 4×4 vehicle with a private driver and expert Explora guide, who join you for the remainder of your itinerary.
Customize Your Itinerary
Want to extend, shorten or further customize your itinerary? Allow us to suggest anything from a six-night adventure to an immersive 11-night itinerary, fully tailored to match your pace, interests, and skill level.
8 Night Itinerary
10 Night Itinerary
Extend your Stay and Enjoy more Time in Atacama
If time allows, we always recommend additional days at the start of Travesía Atacama-Uyuni. These extra days allow for proper acclimatization before progressing to our Ramaditas Mountain Lodge at 13,123 feet (4,000 meters) and Chituca and Jirira lodges at 11,482-plus feet (3,500 meters). It also allows you to more fully experience our expansive Explora Atacama lodge with its Puritama Hot Springs, night-sky observatory, and spa and outdoor pools.

## LODGE
Experience a Collection of Unique Explora Lodges
On Travesía Atacama-Uyuni, adventurous days between Chile and Bolivia on the remote and rugged Altiplano are rewarded with comfort, relaxation and deep rest at a strikingly designed Explora Lodge. Discover the 50-room Explora Atacama in Chile’s famed high-altitude desert before crossing into Bolivia for one-of-a-kind overnights at our three intimate mountain lodges, Explora Ramaditas Mountain Lodge, Explora Chituca Mountain Lodge and Explora Jirira Lodge. Each offers just four to six rooms and a setting amid the volcanoes and high-altitude lagoons of the Altiplano.
At every lodge, experience Explora’s commitment to a sustainable design that prioritizes the environment, dining and meals crafted from locally sourced ingredients, and an invitation to slow down, disconnect, and fully embrace the beauty of the surrounding landscapes.

Explora Atacama
Begin this all-inclusive experience with three nights at multi-award-winning Explora Atacama, our 50-room lodge near San Pedro de Atacama in Chile’s Atacama Desert. More than an ideal place to acclimatize with Explorations across the otherworldly Atacama Desert, enjoy artfully crafted local cuisine paired with bold Chilean wine, an observatory, spa and saunas, and multiple outdoor pools set in the surrounding landscape. Elevation: 8,000 feet (2,438 meters).
VIEW ROOMS
Explora Ramaditas Mountain Lodge
Set amidst shimmering, multi-colored lagoons, our modern four-room Ramaditas lodge Bolivia combines comfortable common areas and Bolivian-sourced materials in the heart of the Altiplano. From here, experience geysers, lagoons, rock formations, ancient trade routes, and vast Andean valleys—along with a striking perch and wall-to-wall windows that invite the landscape in. Elevation: 13,370 feet (4,075 meters).
Explora Chituca Mountain Lodge
Once a lookout for shepherds, our four-room Mountain Lodge in Chituca offers panoramic views of the Altiplano. The surrounding area is rich with ancient settlements, vibrant quinoa fields, and storied villages. Unwind in the cozy lounge and dining area, before retreating to a comfortably minimalist room with stunning views over the distant salt flat. Elevation: 12,244 feet (3,732 meters).
Explora Jirira Lodge
At the foot of the Tunupa Volcano on the northern edge of the Uyuni Salt Flats, our six-room Jirira lodge offers a spectacular view of the world’s largest salt flat. The setting is perfect for exploration: climb the colorful slopes of Tunupa, visit the salt flat’s islands, and discover local villages, wetlands, and nearby archaeological sites. Elevation: 12,077 feet (3,681 meters).
Modern Prefab Design
Explora’s three mountain lodges in Ramaditas, Chituca, and Jirira were designed by Chilean architect Max Núñez. His objective: develop lodging with exceptional minimal impact that raises awareness of the surrounding territory. Discover striking modular designs hoovering above extraordinary places and 100-percent prefabricated and entirely “reversible” construction that allows for future repurposable use.

Embark on Once-In-A-Lifetime Explorations
Designed to gradually unveil the Altiplanos true essence, the Explorations from Atacama to Uyuni offer a progression of unique experiences along this high-altitude route. Travel through three unique zones from the desert to the Uyuni salt flat, expertly led the entire time by an expert Explora guide and experienced driver. Welcome to Explora El Calafate — where ice, wind, and memory converge. Its location balances remoteness with accessibility, providing seamless entry to unforgettable explorations while preserving the untouched beauty of the land.

Every journey blends the iconic highlights with exclusive, immersive experiences — offering a deeper connection to the land’s enduring beauty.

sections.heading: Experiences Customized for You
sections.text:
Experiences Customized for You
Our crafted explorations feature classic routes to iconic sites as well as signature explorations, designed and operated exclusively by Explora.
Select your options to explore to match with your skills and interests. Every evening, you will meet with an Explora guide to tailor the next day’s explorations with your preferences. We also aim to create a personal atmosphere and in-depth discovery by limiting group sizes to no more than eight guests.

sections.heading: Passionate Guides
sections.text:
Passionate Guides
Our guides have an unyielding passion and knowledge for the Patagonian wilderness surrounding El Calafate. Trained at our own School of Guides, these bilingual experts possess a profound connection with the region’s glaciers, steppe, lakes, and estancias. They not only reveal the hidden stories and wonders of this extraordinary landscape but also share our commitment to protecting its fragile beauty, ensuring every exploration respect and preserves Patagonia’s enduring spirit.
Stay tuned! Soon, you’ll be able to discover the full range of explorations we’re crafting to connect deeply with this territory.

sections.heading: Uncover El Calafate's Most Untouched Corners
sections.text:
Uncover El Calafate's Most Untouched Corners
Explore five distinct zones across one of Patagonia’s most remote territories — from up-close encounters with the Perito Moreno Glacier to horseback rides through a historic estancia, deep hikes into hidden valleys, and overland journeys across the open steppe.

sections.heading: 1. Hielos Milenarios
sections.text:
Explore by: Hike Overland Horseback Ride By Boat Mountain Ascent
Explore 24 explorations located in the 5 unique El Calafate zones:
1. Hielos Milenarios
The realm of ice. This zone holds the glaciers of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, one of the largest freshwater reserves on the planet, shaped over millions of years. Glaciar Perito Moreno is its most iconic presence, but far from the only one. Access is exclusively by vessel, making every exploration a privilege: drifting before walls of ice dozens of meters high, listening to the sounds of a living glacier, witnessing a geography that existed long before any human trace and that, in its scale and age, reminds the traveler of their place in the world.
Explore by: 
View Hielos Milenarios Explorations 
2. Valles y Montañas
Where the mountains hold the moisture of the ice fields, the Patagonian forest takes hold, dense, quiet, home to the territory's greatest biodiversity. This zone spans Los Glaciares National Park and the Magallanes Peninsula, a landscape that shifts between forested valleys and wind-exposed summits open to the horizon. Explorations here demand physical effort, but every ascent has its reward: panoramic views of Glaciar Perito Moreno from perspectives few travelers ever reach, and on clear days, the silhouettes of Fitzroy and Las Torres del Paine stretching across the skyline.
Explore by: 
View Valles y Montañas Explorations 
3. Pampa
The Patagonian steppe stretches from the outskirts of Calafate to the Río La Leona — open and windswept. Yet this seemingly desert landscape holds the territory's most ancient geological formations. It was also the stage for the cattle ranching that shaped Patagonian identity, and that history lingers in every rise and fence line. What makes this zone singular is its contrast: the arid vastness of the steppe set against the surrounding masses of water and ice — a geological and visual dialogue found in few places on earth.

sections.heading: Exploration Continues at the Table
sections.text:
Exploration Continues at the Table
At Explora El Calafate, evenings turn fireside. A calm, open-fire kitchen reveals Patagonian flavors as another kind of journey, unhurried and true to its origin. Rooted in Argentine cooking and the tastes of southern Patagonia, dining here invites you to keep exploring. As part of your stay, breakfast, lunch, and dinner are served, with trail meals for long days out and beverages available throughout the day.

sections.heading: Traditional Argentinian Grill
sections.text:
Traditional Argentinian Grill
A fireside parrilla anchors the dining room, and open-fire cooking brings regional tradition forward, plancha-seared trout, roasted vegetables, classic provoleta, and, for those who wish, asado argentino from the grill.
Every thoughtful detail, deepens the sense of place and is included as part of your stay. Vegetarian, vegan, and other preferences are welcomed and prepared with the same care, so every guest can enjoy the parrilla’s fireside rhythm.

Reaching El Calafate is part of the Patagonian adventure. It is accessible by air and road from Chile, serving as the gateway to the vast landscapes and iconic glaciers of Argentine Patagonia.
How to Get to El Calafate
Pick-Up & Drop-Off
EL CALAFATE
From Buenos Aires, Argentina
By Air:
The most convenient way to arrive is via El Calafate Airport (FTE), located approximately 1 hour from our lodge. Regular flights connect El Calafate with Buenos Aires.
From El Chaltén, Argentina
By Road:
We provide ground transportation by van between Explora El Chaltén and Explora El Calafate on select days from October to April.
The trip may take approximately 3.5 hours. Ask availability and conditions to our reservations team: reserve@explora.com
From Torres del Paine, Chile
By Road:
For a more scenic and seamless journey, we offer transfers at preset schedules from our Lodges in Torres del Paine National Park or from the Explora Conservation Reserve.

sections.heading: The Climate of El Calafate Argentina: Where Seasons Shape the Landscape
sections.text:
The Climate of El Calafate Argentina: Where Seasons Shape the Landscape
In El Calafate, the weather is part of the adventure. Located deep in Argentine Patagonia, this remote place experiences all four seasons with striking contrasts — from crisp, wind-swept summers to silent, snow-dusted winters.
Summer (December to February) brings long days and mild temperatures that rarely exceed 20 °C (68 °F). The wind can be strong, sweeping through the steppe and over the turquoise waters of Lago Argentino, but the light is golden and endless — perfect for exploring the glacier, hiking trails and all the explorations we crafted in this part of the world.
Autumn (March to May) paints the landscape with ochre and copper tones. Temperatures cool, the wind softens, and the region becomes quieter, offering a sense of stillness and reflection.
Winter (June to August) transforms El Calafate into a serene retreat. Snow may blanket the landscapes and mountains, creating a peaceful atmosphere where silence reigns and the glaciers appear even more imposing under the pale winter light. On calm days, you will quickly feel warm during the hikes.
Spring (September to November) brings renewal. Wildflowers bloom across the steppe, days grow longer, and wildlife reappears — guanacos, condors, and flamingos return to the shores of Lago Argentino.
Throughout the year, El Calafate’s weather reminds visitors that Patagonia is a land of extremes and beauty. No two days are ever alike, and that unpredictability is precisely what makes it unforgettable.

sections.heading: FAQs
sections.text:
FAQs
WHAT MAKES EXPLORA EL CALAFATE DIFFERENT FROM OTHER HOTELS IN EL CALAFATE?
Unlike hotels in the town of El Calafate, Explora El Calafate is a remote all-inclusive lodge set within the historic Chorrillo Malo estancia, surrounded by the Patagonian steppe with sweeping views of the pampas, the Andes, and glimpses of the Perito Moreno Glacier. The experience goes far beyond accommodation: 30+ guided explorations are included with your stay, led by bilingual expert guides trained at Explora’s own School of Guides. All meals, drinks, transfers, and National Park entrance fees are also included — making it a seamless, immersive Patagonian journey rather than just a place to sleep.
WHAT EXPLORATIONS AND ACTIVITIES ARE AVAILABLE AT EXPLORA EL CALAFATE?
Explora El Calafate offers more than 30 guided explorations across five distinct zones of Argentine Patagonia:
Hielos Milenarios — up-close encounters with the iconic Perito Moreno Glacier, one of the few advancing glaciers on Earth, by boat and on foot.
Brazo Sur — the most remote corner of Los Glaciares National Park, with hidden valleys, lagoons, and glaciers.
Valles y Montañas — forested hikes and panoramic viewpoints where ice, water, and forest converge.
Pampa — overland journeys across the vast Patagonian steppe, tracing the region’s ranching history.
La Estancia — horseback riding and hiking through the lodge’s own historic estancia territory.
All explorations are customized to your skill level and interests, and group sizes are limited to eight guests for a deeply personal experience.

explorations.name: Cerro Cristal
explorations.text: A full-day hike to a summit with open views over the glacial heart of the region. From the top, you can see the eastern face of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field and its glaciers — including the Perito Moreno — and below, Lake Argentino, with that milky blue colour given by rock flour: the fine sediment ground out by advancing ice. The surroundings work as a summary of glacial work: moraines left behind as the ice retreated, meltwater rivers, and young forest growing on newly cleared terrain.

explorations.name: Cara Sur
explorations.text: We sail along a stretch of the Rico River toward the Perito Moreno Glacier, approaching it from a singular perspective. As the boat advances, the southern face of the glacier reveals itself: a wall of ancient ice rising from the water with a presence both silent and overwhelming. An exploration for those who seek to contemplate the glacier without intermediaries, from the water, at the unhurried rhythm of the lake.

explorations.name: Calafate
explorations.text: We explore Laguna Nimez, a small bird sanctuary on the shores of Lake Argentino. Walking its trails, we may discover flamingos, upland geese, and dozens of birds that find refuge in this wetland, and we come to understand the close relationship between the water, the birds, and the town of El Calafate that grew beside it. A serene exploration, ideal for wildlife watching and for understanding how wild and human life coexist on the edge of the steppe.

explorations.name: El Chingue
explorations.text: On this exploration we venture into the Hoya del Chingue area, a mountain range of sedimentary origin that holds an ancient history of the land. We walk along its ledges, reading the passage of time in the layers of rock, while views open toward El Calafate, Cerro Moyano, and Lake Argentino. It is a route that combines geology and sweeping panoramas, where each stratum tells how this landscape was, at different moments, sea, sediment, and finally mountain.

explorations.name: La Tranquera
explorations.text: We ride up to the summer-pasture gate of the Chorrillo Malo estancia, the point where the movement of livestock between the main valley and the upper summer pastures was once controlled. From this place, steeped in ranching history, we begin the return toward the stables with a privileged view of the territory. A horseback exploration that combines estancia heritage and grand Patagonian panoramas.

explorations.name: Perito Moreno
explorations.text: We sail along the Rico Arm of Lake Argentino toward the Perito Moreno Glacier. We disembark to walk along its southern shore, drawing closer and closer to the wall of ice, and then sail again among the drifting icebergs broken off from the glacier. The route culminates at the famous walkways, from which we contemplate the glacier in full perspective. A complete exploration that lets us experience the Perito Moreno from the water, the land, and the heights.

explorations.name: Boardwalks
explorations.text: This is the most accessible exploration for contemplating the Perito Moreno Glacier. Along a system of gentle walkways, we visit various viewpoints and calmly take in the immensity of this wall of ice, alert to the roar of each calving. An exploration designed for those who seek time and serenity to admire one of the most impressive glaciers on the planet, at their own pace.

explorations.name: Península
explorations.text: We climb along the outer edge of the Magallanes Peninsula, gaining height above the Patagonian forest until we overlook the Rico Arm of Lake Argentino. From this privileged vantage point, the Perito Moreno Glacier appears in all its magnitude, revealing its origin in the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. It is an exploration that combines the intimacy of the forest with the monumental scale of the ice, reminding us of the force that continues to shape this part of Patagonia.

explorations.name: La Meseta
explorations.text: We climb along the bank of the Chorrillo Malo, toward the plateau nearest the hotel. Upon reaching its ledge, the landscape unfolds in perspective: the surroundings of the hotel and the historic heart of the Chorrillo Malo estancia are revealed at our feet. From this privileged point we revisit the history of the place, which dates back to its founding in 1906, understanding how estancia life gradually shaped this Patagonian territory. An exploration that weaves together the traces of water, the breadth of the plateau, and the memory of more than a century of history.

explorations.name: Mirador Cristal
explorations.text: We climb Cerro Cristal to understand how water structures and shapes this territory. As we gain altitude, the landscape arranges itself before us: Lake Argentino, Lake Roca, and the Perito Moreno Glacier stand out by their colors and their origins, each telling a part of the region's glacial history. From the summit, the gaze takes in the whole and allows us to read the landscape in its entirety, like a living map sculpted by the ice.

explorations.name: La Condorera
explorations.text: We climb to the ledge of Cerro El Fraile in search of the same perspective with which the condors read this landscape. As we gain altitude, we find traces of their activity —feathers, roosts, and remains— and, with luck, we will see them gliding by our side, masters of the wind. An exploration that brings us closer to the most emblematic bird of the Andes and to the vast horizon it commands each day.

explorations.name: El Fraile
explorations.text: Beside the hotel rises El Fraile, a hill whose geological formations tint the territory with color. We climb its slopes, reading in the rock the layers that compose it, until we reach the summit. From the top, extraordinary views open up and, if luck is with us, we will make out some of the most iconic peaks of Patagonia outlined on the horizon. An exploration that rewards the effort with one of the most complete panoramas in the area.

explorations.name: Brazo Sur
explorations.text: We navigate toward one of the most remote sectors of Los Glaciares National Park, venturing deep into the Brazo Sur arm of Lago Argentino. From the shoreline, we enter the Patagonian forest and push through until we reach the terminal moraines shaped by the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. Here, Glacier Cubo reveals the raw mechanics of glacial dynamics — a territory rarely touched by travellers.

explorations.name: Veranadas
explorations.text: We ride all the way around Cerro El Fraile, traversing the old Chorrillo Malo estancia just as the gauchos did in their work of tending the livestock. The landscape transforms without pause —from the pampas to the forest, and from the forest to the mountain— on a route that encompasses the full diversity of the territory. A horseback exploration that combines tradition, nature, and the unmistakable breadth of Patagonia.

explorations.name: Rio Rico
explorations.text: On horseback we venture into the valley of the Rico River, an old route toward the border traveled by the gauchos on both lawful and unlawful crossings. As we leave the pampa behind and enter the valleys, the vegetation changes and the Patagonian forest envelops us, denser and more humid. An exploration that follows the traces of those who crossed these lands, reading in the landscape the transition between steppe and mountain.

explorations.name: Pastizales
explorations.text: We ride at a walking pace through the pampas and grasslands near the hotel, advancing among erratic boulders and calafate bushes. The route, serene and unhurried, culminates at a lookout with views of the Perito Moreno Glacier, which appears in the distance like a promise of ice. A horseback exploration, ideal for feeling the unhurried rhythm of the steppe and the breadth of the Patagonian landscape.

explorations.name: Chorrillo Malo
explorations.text: We cross the Chorrillo Malo toward the eastern sector of the estancia and gain some height to contemplate the landscape in perspective. We advance at a walking pace, unhurried, enjoying the views of the hotel, Cerro El Fraile, and the pampa that stretches to the horizon. A calm horseback ride that invites us to read the territory from the saddle, at the rhythm of the gauchos who rode it before.

explorations.name: La Frontera
explorations.text: We set out from the hotel toward the southwest, heading for the border with Chile. Following the course of the Rico River, we walk through different ecosystems —from the pampa to the forest— until we reach the “backyard” of the estancia. From there, the Paine massif is revealed on the horizon, and we grasp how close we are to the boundary between the two countries. An exploration that brings together geography, history, and the feeling of advancing toward the edges of the territory.

explorations.name: Las Faldas
explorations.text: We ride across sedimentary plateaus that, in a distant past, marked the level of the ancient Lake Buenos Aires. From this height, the landscape arranges itself in perspective: the hotel at our feet and, in the distance, the Perito Moreno Glacier emerging among the mountains. A horseback exploration that unites deep geology and broad horizons, reminding us how much this territory has changed over time.

explorations.name: Walichu
explorations.text: We visit Punta Walichu, an archaeological site on the shores of Lake Argentino that preserves the traces of the first inhabitants of this land. Its rock paintings —hands, figures, and marks left by hunter-gatherer groups— allow us to glimpse the way they understood and inhabited the Patagonian landscape long before the arrival of the settlers. An exploration that invites us to read the territory through time, recognizing in the rock the oldest memory of the region.

explorations.name: Los Toros
explorations.text: We venture into the Magellanic forest, following the trails left over generations by the herds of bulls and cows that grazed on this estancia. Among the dense woodland we discover hidden nooks where the livestock found shelter from the Patagonian climate, corners that still hold the echo of ranching life. An exploration that interweaves nature and history, revealing how human beings and the forest shared this territory.

explorations.name: Mirador del Chingue
explorations.text: We walk along the slopes of the Hoya del Chingue, a serene route that opens onto sweeping views of the pampa and Lake Argentino. As we advance, the town of El Calafate and its surroundings unfold in the distance, allowing us to understand the close relationship between human beings and the nature around them. An exploration that combines open horizons, the stillness of the steppe, and a glimpse of how life settles on the edge of this Patagonian landscape.

explorations.name: Erraticas
explorations.text: We explore the surroundings of the hotel among erratic boulders—enormous rocks transported and abandoned by the glaciers as they retreated. These silent witnesses, out of place in the middle of the steppe, are proof of a territory in constant transformation. A nearby and accessible exploration that teaches us to read the traces of the ice in every detail of the landscape.

explorations.name: Cerro Moyano
explorations.text: Cerro Moyano tints the surroundings with color and rises as a natural lookout over the territory. We climb to its summit, reading in the rock the traces of a fiery past, until we reach a point where the landscape unfolds without limits: the pampa, Lake Argentino, and, in the distance, the border with Chile. An exploration that rewards the ascent with one of the most complete and singular panoramas in the area.

Brazo Sur — the most remote corner of Los Glaciares National Park, with hidden valleys, lagoons, and glaciers. Valles y Montañas — forested hikes and panoramic viewpoints where ice, water, and forest converge. Pampa — overland journeys across the vast Patagonian steppe, tracing the region’s ranching history. La Estancia — horseback riding and hiking through the lodge’s own historic estancia territory. All explorations are customized to your skill level and interests, and group sizes are limited to eight guests for a deeply personal experience.

faqs.q: What is the best time of year to visit El Calafate?
faqs.a: El Calafate can be visited year-round, with each season offering a distinct experience: Summer (December–February): Long golden days, mild temperatures up to 20°C (68°F), and ideal conditions for glacier explorations and hiking. Autumn (March–May): The steppe turns ochre and copper, crowds thin out, and the landscape feels wonderfully still. Winter (June–August): Snow blankets the mountains and glaciers appear more imposing under pale winter light — a serene, intimate retreat. Spring (September–November): Wildflowers bloom across the steppe, guanacos, condors, and flamingos return to the shores of Lago Argentino. No matter when you visit, Patagonia’s signature unpredictability ensures no two days are ever alike.

faqs.q: How do I get to Explora El Calafate?
faqs.a: The most convenient way to reach the lodge is by flying into El Calafate Airport (FTE), approximately 1 hour from the lodge. Regular flights connect El Calafate with Buenos Aires. Explora includes round-trip airport transfers on preset schedules as part of your stay. Guests traveling within the Patagonia Network can also arrive: From Explora El Chaltén by road (approx. 3.5 hours), with transfers available on select days October–April. From Torres del Paine, Chile by road (approx. 6 hours), crossing the Chile–Argentina border — a spectacular scenic journey. Private transfers are also available at an additional cost.

faqs.q: What is included in a stay at Explora El Calafate?
faqs.a: An all-inclusive stay at Explora El Calafate covers everything you need for a complete Patagonian experience: Accommodation in 20 thoughtfully designed rooms (Standard or Suite) with views of the pampa and mountains All guided explorations — 30+ excursions by foot, horseback, boat, and overland vehicle All meals and drinks — cuisine inspired by local Patagonian ingredients (lamb, trout, native herbs, seasonal produce) and Patagonian wines Spa facilities — outdoor hot tubs to unwind under the open sky National Park entrance fees Round-trip airport transfers according to preset schedules The only things not included are flights, optional private transfers, and personal expenses.

faqs.q: Who designed Explora El Calafate and what is the lodge like?
faqs.a: Explora El Calafate was designed by acclaimed Chilean architect José Cruz Ovalle, with a philosophy of blending seamlessly into the Patagonian landscape. Natural materials, organic forms, and expansive windows frame panoramic views of glaciers, rolling plains, and distant mountains — making guests feel part of the landscape rather than observers of it. The lodge offers 20 rooms — Standard (with views of the pampa and mountains) and Suites — each designed for rest and comfort after a day of exploration. Shared spaces encourage connection: stories shared over exceptional cuisine, a glass of wine by the fire, and the quiet luxury of a hot shower after a day in the wild.

Strategically built within the 14,000-acre Los Huemules Conservation Reserve — our long-standing conservation partners in the region — Explora El Chaltén offers a one-of-a-kind location in Argentine Patagonia. Perched on the Eléctrico River and wrapped in lenga and ñirre forests, the lodge is accessible to nearby Los Glaciares National Park and an ideal base camp for exploring the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, the world’s third largest fresh water reserve.

Explore a remarkable number of diverse ecosystems and three unique regions, with more than 30 guided Explorations and options for self-guided adventure. Must-do Patagonia adventures in this rugged Argentinian region include hikes through forest and rivers valleys to blue lagoons, rock climbing for beginners and experts, birding treks, and challenging high-mountain ascents with views to Mount Fitz Roy.

sections.heading: 1. Los Huemules Conservation Reserve
sections.text:
Explore by: Hike Overland Climbing Self Guided By packraft High Mountain Ascent
Explore a remarkable number of diverse ecosystems
1. Los Huemules Conservation Reserve
The future of conservation depends on shifting our role in the world: from mere observers to custodians – active protectors of the places we explore and are part of who we are. It is rare to find a place on Earth in which so much is packed into such a relatively compact area. The Los Huemules Conservation Reserve, where the Explora lodge in El Chalten is located, encloses features that cannot be easily found elsewhere in Patagonia. This allows travelers to set off on exploration routes from the very doorstep of our lodge, thus minimizing transport and road time. The ecosystems it hosts are as varied as the climates it can witness. A place for introverts, its privacy means you can walk for days without ever seeing another person, walking side by side with nature itself.
Explore by: 
View Los Huemules Conservation Reserve Explorations 
2. Parque Nacional Los Glaciares
The Los Glaciares National Park is an area of exceptional natural beauty, with rugged, towering mountains and numerous glacial lakes scattered within its borders. This area allows travelers to explore a part of the park, encountering the many ecosystems it hosts within. Home to fauna from the sub-Antarctic steppe and woods, the park is a bird-watcher’s paradise, with over 100 species – from the Andean condor to the white-throated caracara – inhabiting the forest and steppe.
Explore by:

items.text: The future of conservation depends on shifting our role in the world: from mere observers to custodians – active protectors of the places we explore and are part of who we are. It is rare to find a place on Earth in which so much is packed into such a relatively compact area. The Los Huemules Conservation Reserve, where the Explora lodge in El Chalten is located, encloses features that cannot be easily found elsewhere in Patagonia. This allows travelers to set off on exploration routes from the very doorstep of our lodge, thus minimizing transport and road time. The ecosystems it hosts are as varied as the climates it can witness. A place for introverts, its privacy means you can walk for days without ever seeing another person, walking side by side with nature itself.

The Los Glaciares National Park is an area of exceptional natural beauty, with rugged, towering mountains and numerous glacial lakes scattered within its borders. This area allows travelers to explore a part of the park, encountering the many ecosystems it hosts within. Home to fauna from the sub-Antarctic steppe and woods, the park is a bird-watcher’s paradise, with over 100 species – from the Andean condor to the white-throated caracara – inhabiting the forest and steppe.

Once a center of conflict between two neighboring countries, the Desert Lagoon (Chile) or Desert Lake (Argentina) is a wildlife enclave around which numerous Patagonian ecosystems can be observed and explored. Framed by lush forests of lengas and ñirres, as well as two minor mountain ranges – the Vespignani range and its hanging glaciers to the west, and the Bosque (Forest) range to the east – this coveted fresh water source spreads over 10 km. from north to south, and approximately 1 km. from east to west. In addition, it’s fed by the Diablo River as well as numerous streams that replenish and maintain the purity of its waters. Naturally, the site attracts substantial wildlife and irrigated varied ecosystems within a relatively small area

sections.text:
EL CHALTÉN
Experience the Cuisine of Argentinian Patagonia
At Explora El Chaltén, gastronomy represents another opportunity to discover the rich traditions of Argentine Patagonia. Open-fire cooking reflects the region’s deeply rooted heritage and takes center stage on the menu in our dining room. Savor fire-roasted beef and lamb as well as seasonal vegetables and tubers roasted in a traditional mud oven. Every thoughtful detail — from the tableware to fresh local ingredients to an impressive menu of Chilean wines — is curated to enhance your immersion and included as part of your stay.

Transfers may be private or shared, with a minimum of two passengers. Private transfers can accommodate up to six passengers. Both routes depart at 9:00 a.m. to allow sufficient time for border crossing. All transfers must be booked in advance, and availability must be confirmed with our reservations team at reserve@explora.com. sections.heading: Climate
sections.text:
Climate
Nestled in the heart of Argentinian Patagonia, El Chaltén is renowned for its ever-changing and dynamic weather. Here, you’ll experience a microclimate where all four seasons can unfold within a single day. Expect clear mornings, sudden bursts of rain, and refreshing winds, all enhancing the region’s dramatic beauty. The landscape, with its striking peaks and expansive valleys, is shaped by this dynamic climate. From sunny afternoons to brisk evenings, the weather in El Chaltén calls for versatile layering and readiness for swift changes, ensuring you’re always prepared to enjoy the breathtaking scenery.

sections.heading: FAQs
sections.text:
FAQs
WHAT EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES ARE AVAILABLE?
All of our guides are Wilderness First Response (WFR) certified, guaranteeing that they have the necessary knowledge and abilities to aid people in remote locations.
In the Park administration, 15 minutes from the hotel, there is a paramedic stationed year round.
For more serious situations there is a hospital in Puerto Natales, 1.5 hours from the hotel, as well as the Clínica Magallanes in Punta Arenas, which is 5 hours from the hotel.
Contact us if you have any questions.
HOW CAN MY RELATIVES CONTACT ME IN CASE OF EMERGENCY?
Telephones (56 2) 3952580, (56 2) 3952581, (56 2) 3952582, fax (56 2) 3952584, or by email recpatagonia@explora.com.
HOW MANY NIGHTS DO YOU RECOMMEND STAYING AT EXPLORA?
We recommend a minimum of five nights to have an exploration experience that allows you to deeply discover Patagonia, although we are sure that when discovering the wonders of El Chalten. Six nights are a good alternative to achieve a more comprehensive knowledge of the area.
CAN I CHANGE THE TYPE OF MY BED IN MY ROOM?
At the time of booking you must select a room with either a king size bed or two double beds. Being in the lodge, if you require, you may change your bed, subject to availability.

explorations.name: Packraft río de las vueltas
explorations.text: Paddle through the Río de las Vueltas on a glacial route shaped by meltwater, passing forested banks and—if skies are clear—the towering Fitz Roy in the distance.

explorations.name: Glaciar Huemul
explorations.text: We take the van to the southern sector of the Lake of the Desert to begin hiking through a rainforest, where we will begin our ascent to Laguna Huemul, at the foot of the Glacier. We will pass through some clearings along the way where we will see the waterfalls that come down from the glaciers. We return along the same trail, with a panoramic view of the Laguna Huemul, Mount Fitz Roy and the Las Vueltas River valley.

explorations.name: Laguna Pollone
explorations.text: We begin by crossing the Eléctrico River and gradually enter a great nothofagus forest, accompanied by Patagonian birdsong the entire time. We then change landscape and move on to the sandy riverbanks of the Eléctrico River, with views of glaciers and mountain ranges up to Lake Eléctrico. We return along the same trail, which will give us other views of the valley.

explorations.name: Rio Arriba
explorations.text: We leave by van northward toward the Laguna del Desierto Provincial Reserve, passing beautiful waterfalls that are formed thanks to the Las Vueltas River Valley's geography. We will cross the nothofagus rainforest until we reach the Lake of the Desert lookout point, which offers a great panoramic view of the lake, the mountains that surround it and their glaciers.

explorations.name: Las Lolas
explorations.text: A brief hike from the lodge will take us to the entrance of the Los Huemules Reserve forest. Along the way are lenga and ñires trees, and lagoons, as well as the company of native birds.

explorations.name: Laguna de los huemules
explorations.text: We hike from the lodge crossing a lenga and ñire forest, watching different types of birds and huemul deer tracks. We hike up to the Azul Lagoon, a water reserve that will reveal what has happened there. Different water birds will follow us along during this hike.

explorations.name: Aves Patagónicas
explorations.text: We leave by van for Laguna Cóndor, where we will be able to observe and learn from the behavior of different types of birds in this region. The sector is home to a great diversity of birds, including some that can only be seen on this trail. We then hike through an ancient rainforest, whose characteristics make it a great place to see different types of owls.

explorations.name: Las Lengas
explorations.text: We hike from the lodge crossing a lenga and ñirre forest, watching different types of birds and huemul deer tracks.

explorations.name: Laguna Cóndor
explorations.text: We will walk through a rainforest area, where biodiversity plays a key role. The route includes a gentle ascent along a rocky ledge, which will give us unique views and perspectives of the Las Vueltas River valley. Diverse birds can be observed in the Laguna sector.

explorations.name: Río Las Vueltas
explorations.text: We border the Las Vueltas River, enjoying different perspectives of the valley and wide views of the Andes Mountains We stop along the way to get different views of the Los Andes Mountain Range.

explorations.name: Reserva Vespignani
explorations.text: We walk along a low difficulty path through the forest of the least known areas of El Chaltén. On the way back, we see the valley surrounded by woody mountains.

explorations.name: La Roca
explorations.text: For those with the appropriate experience, we offer climbing routes for beginners and others that are more demanding, always caring for the traveler’s safety and experience.

explorations.name: Conexión Vertical
explorations.text: We provide a rock climbing briefing that covers the main places to climb in El Chaltén, history, how to control your body, and the importance of trusting partners.

explorations.name: Laguna Cóndor
explorations.text: Un antiguo bosque de Lengas nos da la bienvenida a esta exploración, donde las aves se toman el protagonismo en varios sectores. El trayecto continúa con un leve ascenso por un filo de roca, que nos dará vistas y perspectivas únicas del valle del río de las Vueltas.

explorations.name: Paso del Cuadrado
explorations.text: An ideal exploration for travelers wishing to have a different experience and perspective of the Patagonia.

explorations.name: Cerro Madsen
explorations.text: The ascent to Cerro Madsen, in the Fitz Roy area, is a perfect challenge for beginners in the mountains or for those who want to make their first summit in Patagonia.

explorations.name: Los Valles
explorations.text: We cross the Blanco river valley, then we hike up to the los tres lagoon. Enjoy an impressive view of Mount Fitz Roy.

explorations.name: Lago del desierto
explorations.text: We hike in the northernmost tip of the lake and take a rugged track through the forest, reaching some of the most unexplored parts of this area.

explorations.name: Glaciar Vespigniani
explorations.text: We cross the desierto lake- this historical lake- while enjoying the view of the Vespigniani Glacier.

explorations.name: Laguna de los Tres
explorations.text: We hike through forests and valleys up to the Los Tres Lagoon.

explorations.name: El Pliegue
explorations.text: We begin in the south area of the Los Glaciares National Park, taking a trail to different valleys and a rise with a broad view to the Torre Mount.

explorations.name: Laguna Torre
explorations.text: From one of the accesses to El Chaltén, we hike up a trail and get an ample view to the Torre Mount.

explorations.name: Piedras Blancas
explorations.text: After a hike, we enjoy a view to the Piedras Blancas Glacier while learning about its history, formation, and dynamics.

explorations.name: Huemules
explorations.text: We take a slightly rugged track from the lodge to the Azul lagoon.

explorations.name: Valle de Granito
explorations.text: We walk to the Los Glaciares National Park through a trail surrounded by forests with views to the area’s glaciers.

explorations.name: El Filo
explorations.text: We begin this exploration hiking up the Loma del Diablo ridge, which will give us sweeping views of both the Diablo River valley as well as the Las Vueltas River valley. We will reach a high-altitude ecosystem with a dwarf forest, rocks and sandy banks, where we can register the magnitude of the environment we are in.

explorations.name: Bahía Tranquila
explorations.text: We will border the Desierto Lake, a watershed adjacent to forests.

explorations.name: Mirador Cerro Torre
explorations.text: In this exploration we can observe the marks of a retreating glacier and the impressive Los Andes Mountain Range.

explorations.name: Mirador Fitz Roy
explorations.text: In the Los Glaciares National Park, we cross the forests to get a great view of the Los Andes Mountain Range’s massifs.

explorations.name: Laguna del Diablo
explorations.text: We will hike along a wooded trail overlooking the north face of Mount Fitz Roy. Our route will take us along the Diablo River, the natural habitat of torrent ducks. We will have views of the Cagliero Glacier and the Laguna del Diablo as we will go up.

explorations.name: Valle Eléctrico
explorations.text: The splashing of the Eléctrico River will follow along faithfully during the entire exploration, as we enjoy the contrasting views.

explorations.name: Mirador de las águilas
explorations.text: Views to the Los Andes Mountain Range, the Viedma Lake, and surrounding mountain ranges.

explorations.name: Los Cóndores
explorations.text: A walk that enters the Los Glaciares National Park with a connection and views to the Patagonia.

explorations.name: Corazón de la reserva
explorations.text: We leave the lodge on foot, where we will have a first encounter and connection with the flora and, if lucky, the native fauna of the area. This exploration is a good starting point to understand where we are located within the Los Huemules Reserve and to begin calibrating senses as we hike through ñirre and lenga forests, characteristic of this remote sector of Patagonia.

WHAT ROOM TYPES ARE AVAILABLE AT EXPLORA RAPA NUI?
Explora Rapa Nui offers two room categories: the Raa Suite and the Varúa Room. The
property has 4 suites and 26 Varúa rooms, for a total of 30 rooms. Both room types featurenatural wood interiors, jetted bathtubs, and views to the Pacific Ocean or lodge gardens. Twin or king bed configurations are available in all rooms, and cribs can be arranged on request.
WHAT IS THE RAA SUITE AT EXPLORA RAPA NUI?
The Raa Suite is the premium room category at Explora Rapa Nui, at 44 m² / 474 ft². Each suite features views to the gardens and the Pacific Ocean, a king or twin bed configuration, a jetted bathtub, heating, and a wake-up call service. The suite name draws from the Rapa Nui word for the sun. There are 4 Raa Suites on the property.
WHAT IS A VARÚA ROOM AT EXPLORA RAPA NUI?
The Varúa Room is the standard room category at Explora Rapa Nui, at 32 m² / 345 ft². Each room features views to the gardens and ocean, natural wood interiors, a jetted bathtub, heating, and a wake-up call service. Twin or king configurations are available. There are 26 Varúa rooms on the property. ‘Varúa’ is a Polynesian word meaning spirit or soul.
HOW BIG ARE THE ROOMS AT EXPLORA RAPA NUI?

DO THE ROOMS AT EXPLORA RAPA NUI HAVE OCEAN VIEWS?
All rooms at Explora Rapa Nui have views to the gardens and the Pacific Ocean. The property sits on elevated grassland outside Hanga Roa, with the lodge oriented to take advantage of the island’s coastal landscape. Room views vary by specific location within the property — guests seeking a particular view orientation can request this at the time of booking.

It’s a culture born of resilience, mystery, and a sacred bond with the land. From the iconic moai statues to the ceremonial platforms known as ahu, from ancient villages to the quarry where most of the moai were carved, the island’s archaeological record is tangible at every turn. These remnants come alive through oral traditions passed down across generations.

Journey into Easter Island’s marine world. Rapa Nui’s surrounding waters are crystal-clear and nearly untouched—home to rare marine life and ancient ocean routes. The ocean plays a fundamental role in Rapa Nui’s identity, shaping its traditions, cuisine, and everyday life. The island’s first inhabitants arrived by sea, and its remote location preserved a distinct maritime culture by limiting outside influence for centuries. Thanks to minimal sediment runoff and low plankton levels, the surrounding waters offer exceptional visibility. Dive into underwater cliffs, vibrant coral reefs, and islets that once guided Polynesian navigators—and discover a marine ecosystem defined by remarkable endemism.

How to Get Here
Check-in & Check-out
EASTER ISLAND
How to get to Easter Island from Santiago Chile
From Santiago, Chile, you’ll need to connect to a flight to Easter Island (Rapa Nui), which takes approximately 5 hours.
Upon arrival at Mataveri Airport, our team will pick you up in a van and transfer you to Explora, a short 15-minute journey. Included in programs with transportation. See the location on the map here.
For a private transfer, there is an additional fee. Please contact your reservation agent or email reserve@explora.com before your trip to inquire about availability.
Please note: If you experience a flight change less than 24 hours before check-in and require a private transfer, additional costs may apply.
Check-in & Check-out
Check-in: After 13:00. We recommend arriving at noon for an afternoon exploration.
Check-out: 10:00
We want you to make the most of your stay. That’s why we offer the option of a half-day exploration on your departure day before heading to the airport (if your flight schedule allows). In this case, you’ll need to check out at 07:00 before exploring, and we’ll store your luggage.
*Please note: Lunch service is not included on your departure day and is available at an additional charge per person.

sections.heading: Climate
sections.text:
Climate
Easter Island, or Rapa Nui, enjoys a mild, subtropical climate that remains pleasant throughout the year, making it a great destination no matter when you visit. The average annual temperature hovers around 70°F (21°C), with February being the warmest month, often reaching highs of 81°F (27°C).
Rain is scattered and brief, with an annual average of 45 inches (1,140 mm), but no distinct rainy season, so it’s always wise to be prepared for light showers. The island’s average humidity is about 76%, contributing to its lush green landscapes. Whether you’re visiting during the warmer months or the cooler periods, the gentle breezes and moderate temperatures make it comfortable year-round.

IS EXPLORA RAPA NUI ALL-INCLUSIVE?
Yes. Every Explora stay on Easter Island is fully all-inclusive. faqs.q: What room types are available at Explora Rapa Nui?
faqs.a: Explora Rapa Nui offers two room categories: the Raa Suite and the Varúa Room. The property has 4 suites and 26 Varúa rooms, for a total of 30 rooms. Both room types featurenatural wood interiors, jetted bathtubs, and views to the Pacific Ocean or lodge gardens. Twin or king bed configurations are available in all rooms, and cribs can be arranged on request.

faqs.q: What is the Raa Suite at Explora Rapa Nui?
faqs.a: The Raa Suite is the premium room category at Explora Rapa Nui, at 44 m² / 474 ft². Each suite features views to the gardens and the Pacific Ocean, a king or twin bed configuration, a jetted bathtub, heating, and a wake-up call service. The suite name draws from the Rapa Nui word for the sun. There are 4 Raa Suites on the property.

faqs.q: What is a Varúa Room at Explora Rapa Nui?
faqs.a: The Varúa Room is the standard room category at Explora Rapa Nui, at 32 m² / 345 ft². Each room features views to the gardens and ocean, natural wood interiors, a jetted bathtub, heating, and a wake-up call service. Twin or king configurations are available. There are 26 Varúa rooms on the property. ‘Varúa’ is a Polynesian word meaning spirit or soul.

faqs.q: How big are the rooms at Explora Rapa Nui?
