sections.heading: FAQs
sections.text:
FAQs
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
WHY VISIT ICELAND IN WINTER INSTEAD OF SUMMER?
Winter offers a different set of conditions and activities: glacier hiking with crampons, snowmobiling, and the possibility of seeing the Northern Lights, none of which are available in summer.
WHAT FITNESS LEVEL IS REQUIRED?
The expedition is suitable for all kinds of travelers. The activity level can be adjusted to the group. If necessary, the team can split into two subgroups so each traveler moves at their own pace. No mountaineering experience required.
IS THERE A MINIMUM AGE REQUIREMENT?
Travelers 13 and older are recommended. Exceptions may be considered on a case-by-case basis.
HOW DO YOU MANAGE THE LIMITED DAYLIGHT IN WINTER?
The itinerary is structured around Iceland’s 4–5 hours of daylight. All explorations are planned within that window, and the remaining hours are used for transfers, dining, briefings, and rest.
HOW DO YOU HANDLE COLD AND WINDY WEATHER DURING THE EXPEDITION?
The team adapts the daily plan in real time based on conditions. The itinerary is flexible by design. Technical clothing is recommended for this expedition. Before departure, travelers receive a packing list with everything they should bring.
WHAT HAPPENS IN CASE OF AN EMERGENCY?
In case of an emergency, our team is trained to handle a range of situations. Our guides are certified in first aid and emergency response, and members of our team belong to the Icelandic Association for Search and Rescue, ensuring professional support should an incident arise. We carry communication equipment that allows us to reach emergency services at all times, and evacuation or transfer to a medical facility can be arranged if necessary.

faqs.q: Why visit Iceland in winter instead of summer?
faqs.a: Winter offers a different set of conditions and activities: glacier hiking with crampons, snowmobiling, and the possibility of seeing the Northern Lights, none of which are available in summer.

faqs.q: What fitness level is required?
faqs.a: The expedition is suitable for all kinds of travelers. The activity level can be adjusted to the group. If necessary, the team can split into two subgroups so each traveler moves at their own pace. No mountaineering experience required.

faqs.q: Is there a minimum age requirement?
faqs.a: Travelers 13 and older are recommended. Exceptions may be considered on a case-by-case basis.

faqs.q: How do you manage the limited daylight in winter?
faqs.a: The itinerary is structured around Iceland’s 4–5 hours of daylight. All explorations are planned within that window, and the remaining hours are used for transfers, dining, briefings, and rest.

faqs.q: How do you handle cold and windy weather during the expedition?
faqs.a: The team adapts the daily plan in real time based on conditions. The itinerary is flexible by design. Technical clothing is recommended for this expedition. Before departure, travelers receive a packing list with everything they should bring.

faqs.q: What happens in case of an emergency?
faqs.a: In case of an emergency, our team is trained to handle a range of situations. Our guides are certified in first aid and emergency response, and members of our team belong to the Icelandic Association for Search and Rescue, ensuring professional support should an incident arise. We carry communication equipment that allows us to reach emergency services at all times, and evacuation or transfer to a medical facility can be arranged if necessary. Given the remote nature of this territory and the absence of nearby pharmacies, we strongly recommend that travelers bring an adequate supply of any personal medications for the entire duration of the expedition. Please note that we do not provide or administer medications. If you take prescription medication or have a specific medical condition, be sure to carry everything you may need.

faqs.q: Are the guides local?
faqs.a: Travelers are accompanied by Explora’s expert expedition team throughout the trip. The team also works closely with local partners in Iceland, including drivers and specialized guides for specific activities such as the glacier hike.

faqs.q: What activities are included beyond hikes?
faqs.a: Easy walks, glacier hiking with crampons and ice axes, snowmobiling, and a visit to Sky Lagoon’s geothermal pools.

faqs.q: What vehicles are used during the expedition?
faqs.a: The expedition uses specialized expedition vehicles suited for Iceland’s rugged terrain, plus snowmobiles for specific activities. All transportation during the expedition is included.

faqs.q: How much luggage can I bring?
faqs.a: One suitcase (up to 20 kg / 44 lbs) and a daypack for daily explorations.

faqs.q: Is there Wi-Fi or cell service during the expedition?
faqs.a: Some accommodations have Wi-Fi and signal, but connectivity will be limited in remote areas.

faqs.q: For private groups, can dates be customized?
faqs.a: Dates for private departures must be coordinated in advance. Contact reserveexpeditions@explora.com for details.

faqs.q: Where can I find the detailed itinerary and accommodations?
faqs.a: The full day-by-day itinerary, including accommodations for each night, is available on our website here and on the last page of the downloadable itinerary here.

faqs.q: When does the expedition begin and how do transfers work?
faqs.a: Transfers are available from Keflavík International Airport (KEF) and Reykjavík Domestic Airport (RKV) to the hotel in Reykjavík, coordinated according to each traveler’s arrival time. Check-in is from 3:00 PM. The expedition begins at 5:30 PM at the hotel.

faqs.q: What's included in the price?
faqs.a: Accommodation, all meals and beverages, guided explorations, equipment (crampons, ice axes, snowshoes), all transportation during the expedition, and airport transfers.

faqs.q: What are the departure dates and price?
faqs.a: December 5–11, 2026 / February 22–28, 2027 / March 3–9, 2027. From USD $17,900 per person in double occupancy.

faqs.q: How large are the groups?
faqs.a: Maximum 8 travelers per departure. Private departures are also available.

faqs.q: Do ECHO Society members get any benefits on this expedition?
faqs.a: Yes. ECHO Society members have a 10% discount on this expedition. Contact reserveexpeditions@explora.com for details.

faqs.q: Can I join this expedition as a solo traveler
faqs.a: Yes. Solo travelers are welcome with a single supplement available upon request

faqs.q: How do I book?
faqs.a: You can request more information by selecting your expedition of interest here.

faqs.q: About Explora Expeditions
faqs.a: Beyond Iceland, Explora operates three other expedition programs: the Iceland Summer Expedition, the Tierra del Fuego Expedition (Chile), and the Sacred Mountains Expedition (Peru). All are small-group, nomadic itineraries limited to 8 travelers, with everything included. For dates, itineraries, and booking, write to reserveexpeditions@explora.com or visit explora.com.

text:
## OVERVIEW
An Invitation to Rawness
Experience Explora’s uniquely crafted winter expedition to Iceland — a geological phenomenon still being formed — on an intimate 7-day journey across four of the island’s most elemental territories. Led by an experienced team of expert guides, discover rarely traveled routes through the Golden Circle’s tectonic landscapes, ride snowmobiles onto Eyjafjallajökull’s silent glacier, hike Europe’s largest ice sheet at Vatnajökull, and witness the northern lights illuminate volcanic black sand coastlines, with stays in countryside lodges and the iconic Hotel Borg in lively Reykjavík.
7 Days / 6 Nights
From $17,900 USD
per person in double room

Suitable for all travelers

Private expeditions available
View all departures
Special discounts available for members of our loyalty program Explorer Echo Society.
For more information or reservations, write to us at reserveexpeditions@explora.com or call us at +56 2 23952800.
Itinerary at a Glance
Beginning and ending in Reykjavík, this intimate 7-day winter expedition moves through four of Iceland’s most elemental territories — the tectonic landscapes of the Golden Circle, the volcanic slopes of Eyjafjallajökull, the black sand coastlines of Dyrhólaey, and the frozen expanse of Vatnajökull, Europe’s largest glacier. Days are alive with snowmobile rides, crampons on ancient ice, and icebergs drifting toward the sea at Jökulsárlón. Nights are restorative, with stays at the Art Déco Hotel Borg in Reykjavík, the family-owned Skálakot farmhouse, and the glacier-facing Hotel Jökulsárlón. On the clearest nights, the Northern Lights write the final word.
ITINERARY

REQUEST A QUOTE
The Elements Unbound: A True Winter Expedition
This is Iceland at its most unfiltered. Walk the fractured earth between two tectonic plates at Þingvellir, a UNESCO-protected rift where continents still pull apart beneath your feet. Ride snowmobiles toward the volcanic summit of Eyjafjallajökull — silent now, but far from dormant. Strap on crampons and traverse Vatnajökull, Europe’s largest glacier, reading the ice formations like a map of deep time. Cross a UNESCO Global Geopark, discover two of Iceland’s three National Parks, and on the clearest winter nights, look up — the Northern Lights do not perform on schedule, which is precisely what makes finding them matter.

## ITINERARY
Expedition Itinerary
This expedition constantly inhabits the tension between the rawness of the Arctic winter and the luxury of the essential.
A deep, accesible and transformative experience for curious travelers, not just for experts.
Day 1: Reykjavik
The first night in Iceland is always one of orientation. Hotel Borg in the historic heart — 1930s Art Déco architecture that signals this is no ordinary trip. The group aperitif is the opening ritual: sharing expectations, aligning on the expedition mindset. What strikes most in Reykjavik in winter is the darkness — barely 5 hours of daylight — and the possibility of seeing the Northern Lights from the city itself.
Accommodation: Hotel Borg or equivalent – Reykjavik
Day 2: Golden Circle
An introduction to Iceland’s living geology and history. The earth here is visibly fractured — cracked open along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, still pulling apart. Hot steam rises from fissures in the ground, a reminder that magma sits just below the surface. Towering waterfalls carve through ancient lava fields.
Accommodation: Hotel Skálakot – South Iceland
Day 3: Eyjafjallajökull
Learn about the full story of Iceland’s volcanic activity during the morning, and then approach Eyjafjallajökull by snowmobile —the same volcano that paralyzed European air traffic in 2010—now silent beneath its glacier. If conditions allow, snowshoes take you closer to the summit.
Accommodation: Hotel Skálakot
Day 4: Dyrhólaey
The day opens at Dyrhólaey — a volcanic promontory with Mýrdalsjökull and Eyjafjallajökull rising behind. Then Reynisfjara: black sand, rock spires and Atlantic waves at full force. The day ends at Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon, where icebergs calve and drift slowly toward the sea.
Accommodation: Hotel Jökulsárlón
Day 5: Vatnajökull
As you walk across Europe’s largest glacier with crampons and ice axe, the crevasses and ice formations are a reminder that Earth is alive, still moving, still forming. The day ends at the hotel’s outdoor hot tubs and sauna, to unwind with the glacier on the horizon.
Accommodation: Hotel Jökulsárlón – Glacier Lagoon
Day 6: South Coast
Skógafoss in winter is a different creature — ice clinging to the rock face, rainbows forming when the sun barely clears the horizon. The long drive south is anything but monotonous and Sky Lagoon closes the expedition the way it should — submerged in 38°C geothermal water, while the air bites at -5°C.
Accommodation: Hotel Borg or equivalent – Reykiavik
Day 7: Return Home
The last day is not just logistics. It’s time to absorb what was lived. Check-out before noon. Time for a last breakfast at Hotel Borg. Transfer to Keflavík Airport included at noon.
Accommodation: Hotel Borg or equivalent – Reykiavik

Expedition Departure Dates
We invite you to experience this expedition through a limited selection of departures, each chosen with intention, offering rare access, remarkable landscapes, and the quiet privilege of traveling in a group of just eight. Guided by Explora’s team and certified expedition staff, each journey unfolds with natural ease, allowing space for discovery, connection, and a deeper encounter with a truly untamed territory.

## WHAT TO BRING
What to bring
The temperatures in Iceland’s broad variety of landscapes vary considerably. That is why it’s very important to be prepared when exploring its vast territories. Explora provides trekking poles and a reusable water bottle, and will provide additional personal safety equipment when required during explorations.
Clothing & Layering
Base layer: Breathable top and bottom (merino wool or synthetic)
Mid layer: Thermal fleece or merino
Insulation layer: Down or synthetic jacket
Outer layer: Waterproof and windproof jacket and pants
Long sleeve thermal tops
Trekking pants (thermal or softshell recommended)
Waterproof over-pants
Thermal trekking socks
Footwear
Waterproof trekking boots with good grip (for snow and ice)
Comfortable shoes (for the lodge)
Head & Hands
Warm hat (wool or insulated)
Buff or neck gaiter
Waterproof thermal gloves
Insulated gloves or mittens (recommended extra pair)
Gear
Small backpack (approx. 25L) with rain cover
Sunglasses (UV protection)
Headlamp
Sunscreen (SPF 50 recommended)
Hydration & Essentials
1-liter water bottle (insulated preferred)
Swimsuit (for hot springs)
Shower sandals
Optional but Recommended
Plug adapter (Type C or F)
External battery pack (cold drains batteries quickly)
Cash
Hand and foot warmers
Lip balm with SPF
Moisturizer

Iceland in winter is a territory defined by contrast — between darkness and sudden, luminous clarity. Each departure month carries its own rhythm of light, temperature, and sky.

text:

text:

Once settled in the camp, we take a walk across the areas of the Verde and Blanca lagoons, from where we have a good view of the Licancabur Volcano. The next day we wake up early to begin walking before dawn. We use headlamps to light a well-marked trail. Halfway along the ascent we watch the dawn over the Blanca and Verde lagoons. We reach the summit after walking for several hours. From here, we have a view to the crater and the world’s highest lagoon. Descent can be challenging due to steep slopes and unstable terrain. We cross oldInca ruins on the way back.

text:
We leave the hotel to go to the Mars Valley, where we horseback ride among typical desert landscapes: dunes, reddish sedimentary rock formations and clay grounds. This exploration is perfect to get an idea of the geography and origin of the Salt Ridge.
For experienced and advanced riders only. This exploration is only available for advanced riders who have mastered rising trot and canter over uneven terrain in open spaces and on all types of horses. A test in the hotel is required before going out into the desert. Please note: Not available on Mondays.
Geometric and seemingly infinite, the Atacama salt flat abruptly interrupts the desert’s chromatic continuum.

name: Beter

facts.page_title: Visit the ayllu dunes of Beter, one Atacameño settlement.

text:
In this exploration, we visit the two ayllus, ancient Atacameño farm communities, where we can see the local lifestyle, vegetable gardens and archeological remains. To begin, we will go to the ayllu in Solor. Next we continue to the ayllu dunes of Beter, one of the first Atacameño settlement.
For experienced and advanced riders only. This exploration is only available for advanced riders who have mastered rising trot and canter over uneven terrain in open spaces and on all types of horses. A test in the hotel is required before going out into the desert.
Geometric and seemingly infinite, the Atacama salt flat abruptly interrupts the desert’s chromatic continuum.

name: Rio Salado

facts.page_title: Río Salado: Let's visit an archeological site of great value

text:
We gallop to the Catarpe Valley through the San Pedro de Atacama oasis, towards the Salt Mountain Range. We go through an archeological site of great value and, after lunch, we go down to the Salado River following its course till its confluence with the Grande River. On our way there, we can see petroglyphs. Afterwards we return to Explora.
For experienced and advanced riders only. This exploration is only available for advanced riders who have mastered rising trot and canter over uneven terrain in open spaces and on all types of horses. A test in the hotel is required before going out into the desert.
Geometric and seemingly infinite, the Atacama salt flat abruptly interrupts the desert’s chromatic continuum.

name: Piedra de la Coca

facts.page_title: Discover the Piedra de la Coca, a site with petroglyphs.

text:
We leave by bicycle to Catarpe through a road that goes up to the Salt Mountain Range. We go through an ancient tunnel before starting a descent that will take us to the Piedra de la Coca, a site with petroglyphs. We continue our trip to the Paciencia plains through stony grounds and on our way back we pass through the Mars Valley.
Geometric and seemingly infinite, the Atacama salt flat abruptly interrupts the desert’s chromatic continuum.

name: Ckuta

facts.page_title: Ckuta: Come to bike riding in the Paciencia plains.

text:
We take a van to the Salt Mountain Range and begin bike riding in the Paciencia plains. We travel to the Moon Valley through sandy soil and beautiful landscapes. The return trip is an uneven path that includes different ascents and descents.
Geometric and seemingly infinite, the Atacama salt flat abruptly interrupts the desert’s chromatic continuum.

name: Jirira

facts.page_title: Jirira - Explora Hotels

text:
We will start our hike from the lodge, descending towards the Salar while surrounding the peninsula. We will enjoy impressive views of the Tunupa volcano, walk among a great number of cacti and unique rock outcroppings in the area, as well as see flamingos and the K'ajchi Island. Then, we will round the peninsula to climb up the other side and finally return back to the lodge.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: Isla K´ajchi

facts.page_title: Isla K´ajchi - Explora Hotels

text:
Departing from the lodge, we will head towards the Salar on bicycles. During the summer season, we will pass through the quinoa plantations before entering the Salar through the main entrance. We will experience the unique sensation of cycling through this incomparable landscape with stunning views of the Tunupa volcano. We will arrive at K'ajchi Island, where we will have the option of turning back or walking to the highest point for an elevated view of the Salar. On the island, we will enjoy a snack before continuing our exploration, perfectly timed with the sunset. Finally, we will return to the lodge by bike or jeep.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: Wila Khollu

facts.page_title: Wila Khollu - Explora Hotels

text:
We will start our hike from the lodge towards the summit of Cerro Wila Khollu. Along the way, we will come across a Pirwa, an ancient rock shelter used primarily for storing potato crops, as well as archaeological remains. From the summit, we will enjoy a spectacular view of the Tunupa volcano and the Uyuni salt flats. We will return by the same path until we reach the lodge again.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: Trayecto Overland & Yardangs

facts.page_title: Trayecto Overland & Yardangs - Explora Hotels

text: We will depart by vehicle from Ramaditas towards the Laguna Pastos Grandes area, where we will hike for 4 hours around wetlands and incredible rock formations called Yardangs. It will also be possible to see cave paintings and amazing high-altitude landscapes. We will enjoy lunch with great views before continuing our journey towards the Mountain Lodge in Chituca.

name: Pueblos del Salar

facts.page_title: Pueblos del Salar - Explora Hotels

text:
We leave Chantani by bike and cross sectors with quinoa plantations and different villages. Villages and agriculture can be seen on this route, which passes through Tahua, Chilguilla, Alianza, Caquena and Chiltaico. Diverse wildlife like vizcachas, hummingbirds and butterflies, among others, can be observed.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: Salar

facts.page_title: Salar - Explora Hotels

text:
We leave by bike from the Uyuni Salt Flat itself to Isla Pescado, where we will have incredible and sweeping views of the salt flat and the volcano Tunupa.
*Available starting April 2023.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: QHAPAQ ÑAN

facts.page_title: Qhapaq Nan: Discover Andean wildlife and watch different species

text:
This hike crosses an old trail marked by apacheta rocks that connects two villages. We will be surrounded by Andean wildlife and watch species such as llamas, vicuñas, sheep, and even foxes or pumas. The trail is currently abandoned, but it has existed since Inca and even pre-Inca times.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: KILLA

facts.page_title: Come to see the moonrise (“killa” in Quechua language)

text:
We drive to the Uyuni Salt Flat to see the sunset and then the moonrise (“killa” in Quechua language). The light changes in intensity through the white ocean under our feet, and the sky lightens up in reddish tones. During full moon, the sunset can be seen to the west while the moon rises to the east.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: INTI

facts.page_title: Come to watch the sunrise (“inti” in Quechua language).

text:
We drive to the Uyuni Salt Flat to watch the sunrise (“inti” in Quechua language). The amazing changes in the light cover the immensity of the landscape, and gradually, the temperature rises with the sun, transforming it in a unique experience.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: ANCESTROS

facts.page_title: Pueblos del Salar: Explora Hotels, Explorations, Halfday Tour

text:
This exploration tours small villages that are relatively isolated because they are bordering the salt flat. We begin the tour from the Tajamari River to arrive in Guajala, a farming area with irrigation channels. We then travel to Caquena, a village we can tour and appreciate an Andean ranching. We will also visit a small school in Chiltaico.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: APU

facts.page_title: Apu: Enjoy views to the Tunupa Volcano and the Uyuni Salt Flat

text:
We drive up to a plain with queñoas and llareta moss. This particular type of vegetation grows in high areas, contrasting with the immutable horizon of the salt flat. There will be views to the Tunupa Volcano and the Uyuni Salt Flat while we wander through scarce woods. Several birds follow along.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: LA PUKARA

facts.page_title: La Pukara: Discover this stronghold, is a stone construction

text:
We drive from the lodge to the Salar viewpoint, with views to the vastness of the white landscape. We then have the option of walking to the Pukará. This stronghold is a stone construction that served as protection for villages; there are still vestiges as a token of its role. These buildings are full with the history of Andean peoples.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: TARA

facts.page_title: Tara: discover the Uyuni Salt Flat

text:
We leave by bike and begin to ride until we cross a large section of the Uyuni Salt Flat. We hear the sound of the wheels cutting the salt and far views to the horizon. We arrive in Isla Pescado, to feel the vastness of the surrounding white plains. We return along the same road.
*Available starting April 2023.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: COLORES DEL TUNUPA

facts.page_title: Volcan Tunupa: Explora Hotels, High Mountain Ascent

text:
We arrive in the village of Coquesa to follow a communal route, escorted by a local guide. Up the trail we see the elevated landscapes of the Uyuni Salt Flat. We cross ancient Andean burial sites, a place to see their tomb systems in caves and fabric in vessels. This is an experience with tradition and culture in the area.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: ISLA PESCADO

facts.page_title: Isla Pescado: Discover one of the salt flat’s largest islands.

text:
We will walk across one of the salt flat’s largest islands. A prominent formation with typical Altiplano vegetation to which we climb in the middle of the Uyuni Salt Flat. Gazing towards the horizon gives us a sense of vastness. The typical sound of salt extends below the vast landscape at our feet.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: TRAYECTO ATACAMA – RAMADITAS

facts.page_title: Trayecto Atacama Ramaditas: Enjoy the altitude landscape

text:
The trip from Atacama to the Ramaditas Mountain Home will cross the Altiplano through an active Andes Mountain Range. We leave the lodge and cross towards Bolivia, stopping first at the White Lagoon. We walk along the south border of the lagoon to enjoy the altitude landscape and bird watching.
We then go to the Green Lagoon, from where we walk to the Apachetas viewpoint, where we get a view of the Licancabur and Sairecabur volcanoes. We continue towards the Sol de Mañana Geysers, where the smell of sulfur alerts us of mineral-rich underground currents.
We walk to the lagoons to see amazing flocks of flamingos and other birds. We have lunch enjoying this landscape, the Altiplano, and the Red Lagoon, to then continue with our trip.
It is a rare thing to experience silence on a planet where it seems to have become extinct.

name: CHILTAICO

facts.page_title: Chiltaico: Visit the Pukará, a rock stronghold

text:
We visit the Pukará, a rock stronghold that used to serve as protection for Andean villages. We then descend through the community trail with views to the salt flat and cross crop and grazing lands. During the crop season, we can see crops of quinoa, fava beans, carrots, onions, and potatoes.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: PASTORES

facts.page_title: Pastores: Discover the lifestyles of Andean area’s locals.

text:
This exploration borders the salt flat to reach a shepherds’ area and watch herds of llamas, sheep, and goats. We get to watch estancias and rest areas, some of which are old and others in use at present. A contemplative walk that gazes the rural lifestyles of Andean area’s locals.
For those yearning for a bit more of adventure, climbing the multicolored Tunupa volcano will take you to 17,822 f.a.s.l.

name: Trayecto Overland Salar

facts.page_title: Chituca: Come and see the galaxies, a grotto with peculiar formations

text:
Before heading to Uyuni, we hike up the hills to get a broader view of the surroundings, of the vegetation and of quinoa crops.
We make a stop at San Pedro de Quemes, a village with a marked division between rundown rock buildings and a new area. We then head to Las Galaxias, a grotto with peculiar formations resulting from the emptying of the Uyuni Salt Flat.
We have lunch in the middle of the Uyuni Salt Flat. We walk along one of the islands in the salt flat, the Pescado Island, a formation with typical Altiplano vegetation which we climb in the middle of the Uyuni Salt Flat to admire its immensity.
* If it is not possible to cross the salt flat due to weather conditions, an alternative route will be chosen.

name: ASTRONOMÍA ANDINA

facts.page_title: Atacama astronomy: Discover the cosmos and stars

text:
For all travelers attracted to the cosmos and the stars, Andean skies have unparalleled conditions. Stars and constellations appear with unusual clearness due to minimal light and air pollution. Depending on the season, main visible features are the Southern Cross and Orion. In addition, the Milky Way and its shadows are closely related to the history of Andean people.
Excellent opportunity to further discover the cultural landscapes around it, exploring local villages while also delving further into archaeological understanding.

name: VOLCÁN IRRUPUTUNKU

facts.page_title: Volcan Irruputunku: Enjoy a panoramic view of the Altiplano

text:
We climb the south face of the volcano through a marked trail that surrounds the crater and reaches the north side of the rock. We get a panoramic view of the Altiplano and observe the strong yellow fumarole due to high sulfur concentrations. Along the way, we find a forest of queñoas, a tree that grows at high altitudes.
* Exploration exclusive for programs of 10 nights or more.
Excellent opportunity to further discover the cultural landscapes around it, exploring local villages while also delving further into archaeological understanding.

name: JAWINCHA

facts.page_title: Let's walk from the village of Ikala to the Jawincha.

text:
We walk from the hidden village of Ikala to the Jawincha Valley. Along the way we cross ancient shepherds’ settlements and refuges, as well as quinoa crops. We will also visit a site with petroglyphs and pictographs, vestiges of ancient Andean peoples.
* Exploration exclusive for programs of 10 nights or more.
Excellent opportunity to further discover the cultural landscapes around it, exploring local villages while also delving further into archaeological understanding.

name: LAS APACHETAS

facts.page_title: Las Apachetas: Come and visit Ikala, the "Hidden Village"

text:
We leave the Chituca Mountain Home and make our first stop in San Pedro de Quemes to observe the burned town from above. We then move on to the Jawincha Valley, where we will start to hike along an old trail used by local inhabitants. We then go to the cemetery to visit the museum and tombs. * Exploration exclusive for programs of 10 nights or more.
Excellent opportunity to further discover the cultural landscapes around it, exploring local villages while also delving further into archaeological understanding.

name: PUEBLOS ANDINOS

facts.page_title: Pueblos Andinos: Let's wander through the Valle de las Rocas

text:
We leave the Chituca Mountain Home by jeep and go to the Valley of Rocks for our first hike. We will then continue by jeep to San Juan, where we will walk to the cemetery and its museum, before moving on to Lakaya, considered one of the most important pre-Columbian settlements in the Lípez region.
* Exploration exclusive for programs of 10 nights or more.
Excellent opportunity to further discover the cultural landscapes around it, exploring local villages while also delving further into archaeological understanding.

name: Trayecto Overland Lagunas Altiplanicas

facts.page_title: Trayecto Ramaditas Chituca: discover the changes in the ecosystem

text:
While leaving our Mountain Home towards Chituca we can see the transition from a solitary and extensive Andean expanse to an increasingly friendly geography, which thereby allows for human demography. We will come closer to towns and appreciate the changes in the ecosystem, from areas with scarce vegetation to actively worked fields.
With our driver and guide we cross the lagoons of the Altiplano (Honda, Char Kota, Hedionda), with different views to the volcanoes. We continue until we reach the Turquiri Lagoon, watching diverse Andean wildlife along the road. This lagoon features a large concentration of birds, surrounded by impressive ignimbrite formations.
We walk bordering a grazing wetland for llamas and goats, a haven for one of the traditional trades in the aera. We will then have lunch in the heights of the Turquiri Lagoon with broad views to the Altiplano. We head back to the Mountain Home in Chituca.

name: VOLCÁN ASCOTÁN

facts.page_title: Come to discover the Volcan Ascotan, dubbed the “Ascotán Garden”

text:
We will walk from our Mountain Home, going up through trails surrounded by yareta moss, grasses, and shrubs. As we gain altitude, Honda, Char Kota and Hedionda lagoons will appear. The volcano is acknowledged by colorfulness, due to which it has been dubbed the “Ascotán Garden”. The diverse tones and fullness of the Altiplano have been with us along the entire exploration.
* Exploration exclusive for programs of 10 nights or more.
It is a rare thing to experience silence on a planet where it seems to have become extinct.

name: Yardangs

facts.page_title: Discover Las Catedrales, an ignimbrite geological formation

text:
We leave the Ramaditas Mountain Home and head to the Pastos Grandes sector. We will walk through an area with wetlands until reaching impressive hoodoo-like formations, which we will flank until reaching the petroglyphs. We will see many birds, vicuñas and vizcachas, in addition to hoodoo rock formations, yardangs, and petroglyphs.
* Exploration exclusive for programs of 10 nights or more.
It is a rare thing to experience silence on a planet where it seems to have become extinct.

name: LAGUNA HONDA

facts.page_title: Laguna Honda: Enjoy the Atacama- Ramaditas route

text:
We walk from our Mountain Home up to the Honda Lagoon. The slope towards the lagoon will make us explore the inner passes of the surrounding hills. The flora changes as we go up and yareta moss can be seen in the hills, in contrast with the arid landscapes of the Atacama- Ramaditas route.
* Exploration exclusive for programs of 10 nights or more.
It is a rare thing to experience silence on a planet where it seems to have become extinct.

name: LAGUNA RAMADITAS

facts.page_title: Laguna Ramaditas: Discover the Andean landscape.

text:
We walk bordering the Ramaditas Lagoon, until we get to the canyon that meets the trails along the lagoon. We are surrounded by the Andean landscape. Different birds like eaglets, flamingos, and andean gulls can be sighted, among other vestiges and whispers of Altiplano fauna.
* Exploration exclusive for programs of 10 nights or more.
It is a rare thing to experience silence on a planet where it seems to have become extinct.

name: Lagunas andinas

facts.page_title: Lagunas andinas: visit the Cachi and Pastos Grandes Lagoons

text:
We travel to the Cachi and Pastos Grandes Lagoons, walking along the border of the Cachi or Salada Lagoon, watching vicuñas and flamingos. We then head off to the Pastos Grandes Lagoon, surrounding it to have lunch enjoying the view of the Altiplano landscape and with Andean winds and air.
* Exploration exclusive for programs of 10 nights or more.
It is a rare thing to experience silence on a planet where it seems to have become extinct.

name: Cerro Cristal

facts.page_title: Cerro Cristal - Explora Hotels

text:
A full-day hike to a summit with open views over the glacial heart of the region. From the top, you can see the eastern face of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field and its glaciers — including the Perito Moreno — and below, Lake Argentino, with that milky blue colour given by rock flour: the fine sediment ground out by advancing ice. The surroundings work as a summary of glacial work: moraines left behind as the ice retreated, meltwater rivers, and young forest growing on newly cleared terrain.
Where the mountains hold the moisture of the ice fields, the Patagonian forest takes hold, dense, quiet, home to the territory's greatest biodiversity.

name: Cara Sur

facts.page_title: Cara Sur - Explora Hotels

text:
We sail along a stretch of the Rico River toward the Perito Moreno Glacier, approaching it from a singular perspective. As the boat advances, the southern face of the glacier reveals itself: a wall of ancient ice rising from the water with a presence both silent and overwhelming. An exploration for those who seek to contemplate the glacier without intermediaries, from the water, at the unhurried rhythm of the lake.
The realm of ice. This zone holds the glaciers of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, one of the largest freshwater reserves on the planet, shaped over millions of years. Glaciar Perito Moreno is its most iconic presence, but far from the only one. Access is exclusively by vessel, making every exploration a privilege: drifting before walls of ice dozens of meters high, listening to the sounds of a living glacier, witnessing a geography that existed long before any human trace and that, in its scale and age, reminds the traveler of their place in the world.

name: Calafate

facts.page_title: Calafate - Explora Hotels

text:
We explore Laguna Nimez, a small bird sanctuary on the shores of Lake Argentino. Walking its trails, we may discover flamingos, upland geese, and dozens of birds that find refuge in this wetland, and we come to understand the close relationship between the water, the birds, and the town of El Calafate that grew beside it. A serene exploration, ideal for wildlife watching and for understanding how wild and human life coexist on the edge of the steppe.
The Patagonian steppe stretches from the outskirts of Calafate to the Río La Leona — open and windswept.

name: El Chingue

facts.page_title: El Chingue - Explora Hotels

text:
On this exploration we venture into the Hoya del Chingue area, a mountain range of sedimentary origin that holds an ancient history of the land. We walk along its ledges, reading the passage of time in the layers of rock, while views open toward El Calafate, Cerro Moyano, and Lake Argentino. It is a route that combines geology and sweeping panoramas, where each stratum tells how this landscape was, at different moments, sea, sediment, and finally mountain.
The Patagonian steppe stretches from the outskirts of Calafate to the Río La Leona — open and windswept.

name: La Tranquera

facts.page_title: La Tranquera - Explora Hotels

text:
We ride up to the summer-pasture gate of the Chorrillo Malo estancia, the point where the movement of livestock between the main valley and the upper summer pastures was once controlled. From this place, steeped in ranching history, we begin the return toward the stables with a privileged view of the territory. A horseback exploration that combines estancia heritage and grand Patagonian panoramas.
This is the exploration zone where the Lodge stands, on the grounds of the former Estancia Chorrillo Malo, a territory that has served as a crossroads long before Patagonia had a name.

name: Perito Moreno

facts.page_title: Perito Moreno - Explora Hotels

text:
We sail along the Rico Arm of Lake Argentino toward the Perito Moreno Glacier. We disembark to walk along its southern shore, drawing closer and closer to the wall of ice, and then sail again among the drifting icebergs broken off from the glacier. The route culminates at the famous walkways, from which we contemplate the glacier in full perspective. A complete exploration that lets us experience the Perito Moreno from the water, the land, and the heights.
The realm of ice. This zone holds the glaciers of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, one of the largest freshwater reserves on the planet, shaped over millions of years. Glaciar Perito Moreno is its most iconic presence, but far from the only one. Access is exclusively by vessel, making every exploration a privilege: drifting before walls of ice dozens of meters high, listening to the sounds of a living glacier, witnessing a geography that existed long before any human trace and that, in its scale and age, reminds the traveler of their place in the world.

name: Boardwalks

facts.page_title: Boardwalks - Explora Hotels

text:
This is the most accessible exploration for contemplating the Perito Moreno Glacier. Along a system of gentle walkways, we visit various viewpoints and calmly take in the immensity of this wall of ice, alert to the roar of each calving. An exploration designed for those who seek time and serenity to admire one of the most impressive glaciers on the planet, at their own pace.

Glaciar Perito Moreno is its most iconic presence, but far from the only one. name: Península

facts.page_title: Península - Explora Hotels

text:
We climb along the outer edge of the Magallanes Peninsula, gaining height above the Patagonian forest until we overlook the Rico Arm of Lake Argentino. From this privileged vantage point, the Perito Moreno Glacier appears in all its magnitude, revealing its origin in the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. It is an exploration that combines the intimacy of the forest with the monumental scale of the ice, reminding us of the force that continues to shape this part of Patagonia.

name: La Meseta

facts.page_title: La Meseta - Explora Hotels

text:
We climb along the bank of the Chorrillo Malo, toward the plateau nearest the hotel. Upon reaching its ledge, the landscape unfolds in perspective: the surroundings of the hotel and the historic heart of the Chorrillo Malo estancia are revealed at our feet. From this privileged point we revisit the history of the place, which dates back to its founding in 1906, understanding how estancia life gradually shaped this Patagonian territory. An exploration that weaves together the traces of water, the breadth of the plateau, and the memory of more than a century of history.
This is the exploration zone where the Lodge stands, on the grounds of the former Estancia Chorrillo Malo, a territory that has served as a crossroads long before Patagonia had a name.

name: Mirador Cristal

facts.page_title: Mirador Cristal - Explora Hotels

text:
We climb Cerro Cristal to understand how water structures and shapes this territory. As we gain altitude, the landscape arranges itself before us: Lake Argentino, Lake Roca, and the Perito Moreno Glacier stand out by their colors and their origins, each telling a part of the region's glacial history. From the summit, the gaze takes in the whole and allows us to read the landscape in its entirety, like a living map sculpted by the ice.
Where the mountains hold the moisture of the ice fields, the Patagonian forest takes hold, dense, quiet, home to the territory's greatest biodiversity.

name: La Condorera

facts.page_title: La Condorera - Explora Hotels

text:
We climb to the ledge of Cerro El Fraile in search of the same perspective with which the condors read this landscape. As we gain altitude, we find traces of their activity —feathers, roosts, and remains— and, with luck, we will see them gliding by our side, masters of the wind. An exploration that brings us closer to the most emblematic bird of the Andes and to the vast horizon it commands each day.
This is the exploration zone where the Lodge stands, on the grounds of the former Estancia Chorrillo Malo, a territory that has served as a crossroads long before Patagonia had a name.

name: El Fraile

facts.page_title: El Fraile - Explora Hotels

text:
Beside the hotel rises El Fraile, a hill whose geological formations tint the territory with color. We climb its slopes, reading in the rock the layers that compose it, until we reach the summit. From the top, extraordinary views open up and, if luck is with us, we will make out some of the most iconic peaks of Patagonia outlined on the horizon. An exploration that rewards the effort with one of the most complete panoramas in the area.
This is the exploration zone where the Lodge stands, on the grounds of the former Estancia Chorrillo Malo, a territory that has served as a crossroads long before Patagonia had a name.

name: Brazo Sur

facts.page_title: Brazo Sur - Explora Hotels

text:
We navigate toward one of the most remote sectors of Los Glaciares National Park, venturing deep into the Brazo Sur arm of Lago Argentino. From the shoreline, we enter the Patagonian forest and push through until we reach the terminal moraines shaped by the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. Here, Glacier Cubo reveals the raw mechanics of glacial dynamics — a territory rarely touched by travellers.
The most remote area of the territory. Here we move toward the southern sector of the ice fields, within a valley surrounded by mountain massifs that provide the climatic conditions necessary for glaciers to exist. The cold and humidity of the ice fields allow for a more lush ecosystem, where we find humid forests.

name: Veranadas

facts.page_title: Veranadas - Explora Hotels

text:
We ride all the way around Cerro El Fraile, traversing the old Chorrillo Malo estancia just as the gauchos did in their work of tending the livestock. The landscape transforms without pause —from the pampas to the forest, and from the forest to the mountain— on a route that encompasses the full diversity of the territory. A horseback exploration that combines tradition, nature, and the unmistakable breadth of Patagonia.
This is the exploration zone where the Lodge stands, on the grounds of the former Estancia Chorrillo Malo, a territory that has served as a crossroads long before Patagonia had a name.

name: Rio Rico

facts.page_title: Rio Rico - Explora Hotels

text:
On horseback we venture into the valley of the Rico River, an old route toward the border traveled by the gauchos on both lawful and unlawful crossings. As we leave the pampa behind and enter the valleys, the vegetation changes and the Patagonian forest envelops us, denser and more humid. An exploration that follows the traces of those who crossed these lands, reading in the landscape the transition between steppe and mountain.
This is the exploration zone where the Lodge stands, on the grounds of the former Estancia Chorrillo Malo, a territory that has served as a crossroads long before Patagonia had a name.

name: Pastizales

facts.page_title: Pastizales - Explora Hotels

text:

The route, serene and unhurried, culminates at a lookout with views of the Perito Moreno Glacier, which appears in the distance like a promise of ice. A horseback exploration, ideal for feeling the unhurried rhythm of the steppe and the breadth of the Patagonian landscape.
This is the exploration zone where the Lodge stands, on the grounds of the former Estancia Chorrillo Malo, a territory that has served as a crossroads long before Patagonia had a name.

name: Chorrillo Malo

facts.page_title: Chorrillo Malo - Explora Hotels

text:
We cross the Chorrillo Malo toward the eastern sector of the estancia and gain some height to contemplate the landscape in perspective. We advance at a walking pace, unhurried, enjoying the views of the hotel, Cerro El Fraile, and the pampa that stretches to the horizon. A calm horseback ride that invites us to read the territory from the saddle, at the rhythm of the gauchos who rode it before.
This is the exploration zone where the Lodge stands, on the grounds of the former Estancia Chorrillo Malo, a territory that has served as a crossroads long before Patagonia had a name.

name: La Frontera

facts.page_title: La Frontera - Explora Hotels

text:
We set out from the hotel toward the southwest, heading for the border with Chile. Following the course of the Rico River, we walk through different ecosystems —from the pampa to the forest— until we reach the “backyard” of the estancia. From there, the Paine massif is revealed on the horizon, and we grasp how close we are to the boundary between the two countries. An exploration that brings together geography, history, and the feeling of advancing toward the edges of the territory.
This is the exploration zone where the Lodge stands, on the grounds of the former Estancia Chorrillo Malo, a territory that has served as a crossroads long before Patagonia had a name.

name: Las Faldas

facts.page_title: Las Faldas - Explora Hotels

text:
We ride across sedimentary plateaus that, in a distant past, marked the level of the ancient Lake Buenos Aires. From this height, the landscape arranges itself in perspective: the hotel at our feet and, in the distance, the Perito Moreno Glacier emerging among the mountains. A horseback exploration that unites deep geology and broad horizons, reminding us how much this territory has changed over time.
This is the exploration zone where the Lodge stands, on the grounds of the former Estancia Chorrillo Malo, a territory that has served as a crossroads long before Patagonia had a name.

name: Walichu

facts.page_title: Walichu - Explora Hotels

text:
We visit Punta Walichu, an archaeological site on the shores of Lake Argentino that preserves the traces of the first inhabitants of this land. Its rock paintings —hands, figures, and marks left by hunter-gatherer groups— allow us to glimpse the way they understood and inhabited the Patagonian landscape long before the arrival of the settlers. An exploration that invites us to read the territory through time, recognizing in the rock the oldest memory of the region.
The Patagonian steppe stretches from the outskirts of Calafate to the Río La Leona — open and windswept.

name: Los Toros

facts.page_title: Los Toros - Explora Hotels

text:
We venture into the Magellanic forest, following the trails left over generations by the herds of bulls and cows that grazed on this estancia. Among the dense woodland we discover hidden nooks where the livestock found shelter from the Patagonian climate, corners that still hold the echo of ranching life. An exploration that interweaves nature and history, revealing how human beings and the forest shared this territory.
This is the exploration zone where the Lodge stands, on the grounds of the former Estancia Chorrillo Malo, a territory that has served as a crossroads long before Patagonia had a name.

name: Mirador del Chingue

facts.page_title: Mirador del Chingue - Explora Hotels

text:
We walk along the slopes of the Hoya del Chingue, a serene route that opens onto sweeping views of the pampa and Lake Argentino. As we advance, the town of El Calafate and its surroundings unfold in the distance, allowing us to understand the close relationship between human beings and the nature around them. An exploration that combines open horizons, the stillness of the steppe, and a glimpse of how life settles on the edge of this Patagonian landscape.
The Patagonian steppe stretches from the outskirts of Calafate to the Río La Leona — open and windswept.

name: Erraticas

facts.page_title: Erraticas - Explora Hotels

text:
We explore the surroundings of the hotel among erratic boulders—enormous rocks transported and abandoned by the glaciers as they retreated. These silent witnesses, out of place in the middle of the steppe, are proof of a territory in constant transformation. A nearby and accessible exploration that teaches us to read the traces of the ice in every detail of the landscape.
This is the exploration zone where the Lodge stands, on the grounds of the former Estancia Chorrillo Malo, a territory that has served as a crossroads long before Patagonia had a name.

name: Cerro Moyano

facts.page_title: Cerro Moyano - Explora Hotels

text:
Cerro Moyano tints the surroundings with color and rises as a natural lookout over the territory. We climb to its summit, reading in the rock the traces of a fiery past, until we reach a point where the landscape unfolds without limits: the pampa, Lake Argentino, and, in the distance, the border with Chile. An exploration that rewards the ascent with one of the most complete and singular panoramas in the area.
The Patagonian steppe stretches from the outskirts of Calafate to the Río La Leona — open and windswept.

text:

If clouds allow, the Fitz Roy Massif appears on the horizon as we navigate past riverside forests and the silent presence of aquatic birds. The river takes shape from a network of streams that carry glacial meltwater down from the heights, linking the ice with the southern valleys.

name: Tangata Manu

facts.page_title: Tangata Manu | Birdman Kayak Route | Explora Easter Island

text:
Paddle along the legendary coastline that gave rise to the Birdman ritual. From Hanga Piko, navigate toward the islets of Motu Nui, Motu Iti, and Motu Kao Kao—once the finish line of a daring ocean challenge where competitors swam to retrieve a single egg that would crown a new leader. Surrounded by steep cliffs, seabirds, and the unpredictable Pacific, this journey reveals the dramatic setting of one of Rapa Nui’s most powerful ancestral rites.
Journey into Easter Island’s marine world.

name: Maratiri

facts.page_title: Kayak Exploration along Rapa Nui’s Eastern Coast - Explora Hotels

text:
This kayaking exploration follows one of the most powerful stretches of coastline on Rapa Nui’s eastern shore. Departing from Hanga Nui, with constant views of Ahu Tongariki, we navigate toward the remote Motu Maratiri along an open bay shaped by wind and ocean. This same coastline was described by Captain Cook during the era when the moai lay fallen, offering a rare historical perspective from the sea. A journey that connects landscape, history, and the calm presence of Rapa Nui’s eastern coast.
Journey into Easter Island’s marine world.

name: Ariki

facts.page_title: Kayak Exploration from Anakena to Ovahe - Explora Lodges

text:
This kayak exploration follows one of the most symbolic stretches of Easter Island's coast. Starting from Anakena, believed to be the landing site of the island’s first Polynesian settlers, we paddle toward Ovahe through calm, clear waters. The route connects two iconic beaches and offers insight into the island’s origins, its connection to the ocean, and ancestral navigation traditions.
Journey into Easter Island’s marine world.

name: Motu Nui

text:
We leave the lodge by van to the fishermen's cove in Hanga Roa. From there we take a boat southwest, flanking the coast to see the caves in the area and then observe the cliffs of Rano Kau and surrounding areas. We then go to Motu Kao Kao, where we will flank the area to observe the transparency of the water and the volcanic formations of the islets. The islets are bird sanctuaries, meaning that where we will be able to observe the largest number of bird species on the island.
Journey into Easter Island’s marine world.

name: La Peninsula

text:

Discover the island’s dramatic landscapes.

name: The Hills

facts.page_title: The Hills: Enjoy the contrasting landscapes of Easter Island.

text:
In this exploration we’ll see the contrasting landscapes of Easter Island. We first ride up to the Terevaka, enjoy the view and then ride down to Ahu Akivi. Then, we head to Ahu Tepeu, a site with different archaeological remains. We continue to Hanga Roa and ride along the south coastline enjoying a view to the ocean. We return by bike.
Discover the island’s dramatic landscapes.

name: Rano Kau

facts.page_title: Let's hike to the crater of the Rano Kau Volcano.

text:
We start in Ahu Tahira, a construction platform with perfectly overlapping rock structures. We begin hiking to the crater of the Rano Kau Volcano and Orongo. This is the ancient ceremonial village where Birdman competitions used to take place. We head down south by bike and ride along the coast visiting several archaeological sites. We keep on going to Explora.
Discover the island’s dramatic landscapes.

name: Snorkeling Bird islets

facts.page_title: Snorkeling Bird islets: Come to snorkel around the Motus

text:

Journey into Easter Island’s marine world.

name: Snorkeling Motu Tautara

facts.page_title: Snorkeling Motu Tautara: Come to see corals and marine fauna

text:
Departure by van from the lodge to the Hanga Roa cove, where we take a boat north to the Motu Tautara, an islet that is located very close to the island and in front of Ana Kakenga, a cave also known as two windows. During the boat trip you can appreciate a different view of the Tahai complex, as well as other archaeological sites located on the northwest coast of the island. The area where the Motu Tautara is located is part of a protected coastal marine area in which corals and a diversity of marine fauna can be seen, in addition to endemic species.
Journey into Easter Island’s marine world.

name: Discover Scuba Diving

facts.page_title: Discover Scuba Diver: to know Rapa Nui’s submarine world.

text:
This exploration is the easiest way to get to know Rapa Nui’s amazing submarine world. name: Hanga

facts.page_title: Hanga: Discover a magnetic stone to Rapa Nui’s origins

text:

We hike (1) and go by a cove and continue hiking up to Tepito Kura, a site featuring a huge tumbled moai and a magnetic stone associated to Rapa Nui’s origins. We continue by van to Anakena, the landing area of the first Polynesian settlers (2). Time to enjoy the beach. Bring your swimsuit.

name: Pukao

facts.page_title: Come exploration of the Pukao (“top knot” in Rapa Nui)

name: Lago Gutierrez

facts.page_title: Lago Gutierrez - Explora Hotels

text:
This walking route recreates the ancient pathways of the Aonikenk, hunter-gatherers of Patagonia who roamed the pampas of the Chacabuco Valley thousands of years ago. Their traces endure in the petroglyphs of the Cueva de los Niños, located near the trail. The route culminates at Lago Gutiérrez, the largest in the Chacabuco Valley, which served as a resting site for the long journeys of nomadic Patagonian communities.
For the troperos - traditional nomadic herders - and ranchers of the region, the year was divided into two key seasons: the "veranada" and the "invernada. During the summer, the troperos drove their cattle to the veranadas, high pastures that, once free of snow, provided abundant grazing in clearings surrounded by deciduous forests of ñirre and lenga. In winter, the herds moved to the winter pastures, lower, sheltered areas where corrals provided protection from inclement weather. Today, thanks to the ecological restoration efforts led by Rewilding Chile, these clearings and ancient forests used for cattle grazing have been transformed into a natural sanctuary waiting to be explored.

For the troperos - traditional nomadic herders - and ranchers of the region, the year was divided into two key seasons: the "veranada" and the "invernada. During the summer, the troperos drove their cattle to the veranadas, high pastures that, once free of snow, provided abundant grazing in clearings surrounded by deciduous forests of ñirre and lenga. In winter, the herds moved to the winter pastures, lower, sheltered areas where corrals provided protection from inclement weather. Today, thanks to the ecological restoration efforts led by Rewilding Chile, these clearings and ancient forests used for cattle grazing have been transformed into a natural sanctuary waiting to be explored.

The origin of all life lies in water. The action of glaciers, erosion, and more recently, streams and rivers like the Cochrane and Baker, have shaped a landscape that supports remarkable biodiversity. This environment is home to evergreen forests, birds like the Magellanic woodpecker, intricate fungal networks, and the elusive huemul, southern Andean deer. Explore its glacier-fed rivers, with their turquoise hues, lakes, and wetlands that sustain this intricate web of life. Over time, human history has also intertwined with this vibrant ecosystem, sharing in and evolving alongside it.

text:
The Cañadón de las Torres exploration takes its name from the landscape that defines it: a wide, open canyon that draws the gaze toward the imposing Torres, ever-present protagonists that set the course of the journey.
More than a horseback ride, it is an invitation to traverse a territory in transformation. Here, ancient grazing lands are slowly giving way to the regeneration of native forest, a silent process that reveals itself with every stretch of the trail.
At an unhurried pace, we ride through wetlands, small lagoons, and natural viewpoints. The Torres appear and disappear beyond the hills, guiding the way and offering a constant reminder of the scale of the landscape we move through.
The gaucho and Patagonia are one, sharing temperance, silence, mystery and fascination.

name: Horizonte

facts.page_title: Patagonia Full Day Hike - Explora Hotels

text:
We drive to the Torres del Paine Conservation Reserve, located in the northeastern side of the national park. Our hike begins near the old estancia buildings, gradually ascending the slopes of the Obelisco hill and Punta Hermandad. The trail takes us from the Patagonian steppe through patches of shrubland and lenga forests, in an increasingly scenic setting.
As we gain elevation, panoramic views open to the south: wetlands, rivers, and vast steppe plains framed by the Paine Massif, with the iconic three Towers standing out in the distance. To the north, the towering rock walls of the Obelisco hill dominate the landscape, showcasing dramatic sediment layers and condor roosting sites. After taking in this monumental scenery, we begin our descent and return to the lodge by van.

Step directly into Explora’s private 6,000-hectare Conservation Reserve — a protected territory that connects Torres del Paine National Park with broader Patagonian landscapes. facts.page_title: Ferrier: Enjoy panoramic views of the Grey and Pehoé lakes.

text:
We travel by van to the Grey Lake where we begin a demanding ascent during which we get views of the Lake and the huge ice mass of the South Ice Fields. We cross a forest and continue to the top with panoramic views of the Grey and Pehoé lakes. We descend and return by van.
Forests disavow man made borders. Instead, drawing their own horizons – crossing mountains, skipping lakes and covering entire territories with patient vertical contemplation.

name: VALLE DEL FRANCÉS

facts.page_title: Enjoy the trekking from the Paine Grande to the Valle del Frances

text:
We cross the Pehoé Lake by catamaran to the Paine Grande refuge where we start the trek. We enter the Francés Valley through a forest, cross the suspension bridge over the Francés River and continue to the Italian Camp. From there, we see the glacier and the granite peaks that frame the area. We return by the same trail.
*Navigation is subject to weather.
Glaciers are monuments of time. Patient titans of nature whose fragile presence is in great measure responsible for the geographic spectacle of Patagonia.

name: GLACIAR GREY

facts.page_title: Come and enjoy the Grey Glacier and the Southern Ice Fields

text:
We cross the Pehoé Lake by catamaran to the Paine Grande refuge to cross one of the stretches of the W. Around the midpoint of the hike, we can see the Grey Glacier and the Southern Ice Fields. We continue walking to the beach of Grey Lake where we board a boat that brings us to the glacier and then leaves us on the other side of the lake. We walk along the beach and through a forest to the van.
*Navigation is subject to the availability of Explora's external operator and the weather.
*For safety reasons, this exploration is available only between the months of September and April.
Glaciers are monuments of time. Patient titans of nature whose fragile presence is in great measure responsible for the geographic spectacle of Patagonia.

name: ALTO DEL TORO

facts.page_title: Come and discover Alto del Toro and enjoy unparalleled views.

text:
We travel by van to a steep path facing the Paine River. We begin our trek towards the mountain range passing through an old forest. We continue ascending to an overlook with unparalleled views of the Paine massif and the lakes that surround it. Then, we begin the descent towards the van.
The intersection, the estuary, the frontier. Sometimes the collision of two worlds is a world in itself.

name: Baguales

facts.page_title: Baguales - Explora Hotels

text:
An overland journey into the Sierra Baguales through some of the most remote landscapes in Patagonia. Along the route, mountains and ravines reveal different layers of the area's history, until reaching Estancia Las Cumbres.
From there, we walk through the surrounding terrain to grasp the scale and remoteness of this territory.
Venture into one of Patagonia’s most remote and least explored territories. Located northeast of the Conservation Reserve, near the border between Chile and Argentina, Sierra Baguales is a landscape of ancient geological formations, vast open valleys, and fossils that predate the Andes themselves — a place where the earth’s oldest chapters surface with every season.Hike through interior valleys, climb to natural viewpoints, and cross the region overland to reach lagoons, cerros, and panoramic horizons that reveal the deep geological history of the land. Wildlife moves freely across these plains, and the sense of remoteness is almost absolute. This is Patagonia with the volume turned down — and the scale turned all the way up.

facts.page_title: Vuelta a Baguales - Explora Hotels

From here, the Torres del Paine are also visible on the horizon, part of a landscape steeped in history.

name: Mirador del Obelisco

facts.page_title: Patagonia Full Day Hike - Explora Hotels

text:
We drive to the Torres del Paine Conservation Reserve, located in the northeastern side of the national park. Our hike begins near the old estancia buildings, gradually ascending the slopes of the Obelisco hill and Punta Hermandad. The trail takes us from the Patagonian steppe through patches of shrubland and lenga forests, in an increasingly scenic setting.
As we gain elevation, panoramic views open to the south: wetlands, rivers, and vast steppe plains framed by the Paine Massif, with the iconic three Towers standing out in the distance. To the north, the towering rock walls of the Obelisco hill dominate the landscape, showcasing dramatic sediment layers and condor roosting sites. After taking in this monumental scenery, we begin our descent and return to the lodge by van.
The gaucho and Patagonia are one, sharing temperance, silence, mystery and fascination.

name: Encuentros con el Puma

facts.page_title: Encuentros con el Puma - Explora Hotels

text:
An exploration that invites you to observe, in a responsible manner, pumas in their natural habitat. Accompanied by expert guides, we explore the sweeping landscapes of Patagonia with the possibility of encountering this emblematic feline.
Conducted in partnership with specialized external services, subject to availability.
Discover the southeastern sector of Torres del Paine National Park — an open territory of Patagonian steppe and interconnected lakes, where wildlife, wetlands, and sweeping views of the massif define the landscape. This is the part of the park where the horizon opens up, and where the life of Patagonia reveals itself in slower, more intimate ways. Explore on foot or overland through sectors like Laguna Azul, Lago Sarmiento, and Laguna Amarga, along with wetlands such as Vega Castillo. Follow wildlife corridors where guanacos graze freely, spot extraordinary birdlife, and walk landscapes where the granite towers appear on the horizon like a distant, watchful presence.

Starting with a scenic train ride to the trailhead, the journey unfolds through lush cloud forests, over ancient stone steps and through timeless mountain tunnels, culminating in an awe-inspiring arrival at the Sun Gate (Inti Punku) - the grand entrance to the legendary Machu Picchu, just as the Incas experienced it centuries ago.

We continue walking through Ollantaytambo, ascending a path with vegetation next to houses and orchards. text:

We leave the hotel towards the train station in Ollantaytambo, where we take the train to the town of Aguas Calientes to ascend to Machu Picchu by bus. We explore this magical place for approximately three hours. This version does not include the hike to Puerta del Sol or Inti Punku. Once we’ve visited the sanctuary, we leave Machu Picchu and head towards the station to take the train back.

name: Huchuy Qosqo

facts.page_title: Join us the Palacios de Huchuy Qosqo, down an Inca trail

text:
This exploration offers breathtaking views to lagoons at different altitudes, to the farmlands of Chinchero and to the valleys. To reach the remains of the Huchuy Qosqo Palaces, it goes down an Inca trail. Once in the remains, you cannot miss lying down in the gardens, taking a rest and enjoying the view towards Sacred Valley.
This highly dynamic zone is a feast to the eyes that varies significantly depending on the seasons and harvesting times.

name: Pachatusan

facts.page_title: Come and see Cerro Pachatusan, the protector of the world.

text:
We begin our ascent by a path of agricultural and livestock use. During this exploration, we can see Cerro Pachatusan, considered in Inca culture to be the protector of the world. We walk to an open area with wide views of the Cusco Valley and finally, we descend to the archaeological centers of Pukara and Tipón, where agriculture was developed with an important Inca hydraulic system that is still in use today.
This highly dynamic zone is a feast to the eyes that varies significantly depending on the seasons and harvesting times.

name: Rio Urubamba

facts.page_title: Rio Urubamba: Discover a quiet area of cornfields

text:
The road used for this exploration goes down the south side of the Urubamba River, a quiet area of cornfields, old haciendas and manors from the 19th and 20th centuries. This bike ride is recommended for families wishing to take a long walk or for those who want to take on a sport.
Following the winding course of the Urubamba River, this area showcases Inca architecture at its best, enclosing some of Peru’s most important archaeological landmarks, from Pisac to Macchu Picchu.

name: Cuesta del Sapo

facts.page_title: Cuesta del Sapo: The road offers very interesting views come and enjoy

text:
From the heights of the Sacred Valley’s slopes we descend over a track in good conditions. The road offers very interesting views to the mountains and the Urubamba river. Once downhill, we will continue bordering the river through an area of cornfields and orchards and densely packed Inca terraces.
Following the winding course of the Urubamba River, this area showcases Inca architecture at its best, enclosing some of Peru’s most important archaeological landmarks, from Pisac to Macchu Picchu.

name: Huayna Kolka

facts.page_title: Let's enjoy the viewpoint of Huayna Kolka

text:
After visiting the archaeological site of Machu Kolka, we get on our bikes and begin a descent among trees and adobe houses towards the town of Racchi. There, we pedal in ascent towards the viewpoint of Huayna Kolka to contemplate the valley. We descend by a winding dirt road to Huayllabamba. At this point, we skirt around different crop fields until we reach explora.
This zone showcases the valley’s verticality – a pivotal component around which the Incas developed their particular cosmovision.

name: Huaypo Views

facts.page_title: Huaypo Views: Explora Hotesl, Expeditions, Full day Bike

text:
This exploration crosses small farms and villages of Chinchero. It takes the traveler to the remains of the Moray experimental crop center, the colonial town of Maras and its Inca salt-mines, to finalize with a descent to the Urubamba River. This exploration is recommended for travelers in good physical conditions and experienced in mountain biking.
This zone showcases the valley’s verticality – a pivotal component around which the Incas developed their particular cosmovision.
